detail.abstract: Is the EU's ambition to diversify its green energy sources in order to support the green transition adequately supported by its corporate sustainability law and external relations law? In this paper, we explore those two questions using the case of the EU's attempt to secure the supply of critical raw material lithium and its exploitation through a memorandum of understanding with Serbia, an EU candidate state where a considerable popular mobilization against the project exists. We find that the limitations in the EU's corporate sustainability framework limit the minimization of the project's impact to people and the environment. Additionally, we find that the enlargement conditionality in the case of Serbia failed to adequately position the substantive and procedural environmental law safeguards and that, consequentially, the rule of law in environmental matters in Serbia was never elevated to the stature that it deserves given the important challenges that this area brings. We argue for a more inclusive, democratic action that would remedy these two shortcomings.

title: Development of an Advanced ANN-CA Framework to Model Urban Expansion and Thermal Variations in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

detail.title: Development of an Advanced ANN-CA Framework to Model Urban Expansion and Thermal Variations in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
detail.abstract: Rapid urban development in Kuala Lumpur (KL) has significantly contributed to the reduction of urban green spaces (UGS), leading to a notable increase in land surface temperature (LST). This study aims to predict UGS changes and their impact on LST for the year 2025 using an Artificial Neural Network-Cellular Automaton (ANN-CA) model. The model was calibrated based on land-use data from 2014 to 2019 and demonstrated a high prediction accuracy with 93% for land-use changes and 94% for LST distribution, validated through the Kappa index. The results predict a substantial expansion of built-up areas (BUA), covering approximately 78.65% of KL, while UGS and water bodies (WBA) are expected to decline to 20.01% and 1.34%, respectively. The maximum LST is projected to reach 40.99°C by 2025, representing a 6°C increase from 2019. The findings highlight the critical need for effective UGS conservation strategies and land-use policies to mitigate urban heat and enhance sustainability in KL. This study offers valuable insights for urban planners and policymakers in designing adaptive measures to address the challenges of urban heat islands (UHI).

title: Algorithmic Exclusion in Automated Resource Allocation: Contestability and Accountability in Climate-Vulnerable Contexts

detail.abstract: Automated decision systems increasingly mediate how climate adaptation resources, insurance payouts, and humanitarian support are targeted in climate-vulnerable contexts. This article develops the concept of algorithmic exclusion: the marginalisation of communities from the governance architecture that produces allocative decisions, not only from its outputs. Drawing on science and technology studies, algorithmic accountability, and data justice, the article identifies three mutually reinforcing mechanisms: datafication asymmetry, institutional displacement, and contestability failure. These mechanisms interact as a loop: misrepresentation acquires allocative authority, and the absence of contestation prevents correction. Using theory-building documentary analysis across four categories, data architecture, institutional authority, affected-user understanding, and grievance/redress capacity, the article examines Bangladesh's satellite-based Index-Based Flood Insurance (IBFI) scheme. Published field-based evidence from Aheeyar et al. (2019a, 2019b), drawing on surveys, focus groups, and interviews with 220 enrolled and non-enrolled farmers, supports the analysis by documenting farmer understanding, basis-risk concerns, and grievance-redress gaps; only 35 per cent of farmers could explain how the insurance product worked. The article proposes the Framework for Equitable Algorithmic Governance (FEAIG), linking each mechanism to safeguards for intelligibility, participatory validation, local review authority, grievance redress, and adaptive oversight. The contribution is a theory-building model for assessing automated resource allocation as a sociotechnical governance problem whose technical performance and procedural legitimacy can diverge.

title: Demand for Conversational AI
affiliations: ETH Zürich, University of Barcelona - Institut d'Economia de Barcelona (IEB) and Sapienza University of Rome

detail.title: Demand for Conversational AI

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: "The market for conversational AI companions is booming, yet by standard stated-preference and welfare measures relational AI appears barely demanded. Using a preregistered, within- respondent conjoint experiment in a U.S. online sample (N = 1,989), we estimate demand across five purposes (administrative assistance, studying, wellness, friendship, and romance). Purpose dominates interest, instrumental uses rank highest, romance lowest, and the gradient is corroborated by Google Trends and anonymized ChatGPT usage data. Free pricing raises interest sharply but is attenuated for relational purposes, revealing non-monetary signaling costs that price reductions cannot eliminate; privacy and personalization shift demand, while interaction modality does not. Second-order beliefs exceed own interest in proportion to the purpose penalty, consistent with a single stigma parameter suppressing stated below latent demand. Recovering this suppression, corrected consumer surplus for a free romantic companion turns positive, the welfare mirror image of social media’s collective trap, with the externality sign reversed and a low-adoption rather than over-adoption equilibrium. Because we identify only the individual suppression component, this correction is a lower bound. A complementary hierarchical Bayes structural demand model recovers the full distribution of individual willingness to pay and embeds respondent-level signaling sensitivity as a structural covariate: social-image suppression loads specifically on relational purpose coefficients (Romantic: −0.841 per SD; Friend: −0.683 per SD) while leaving price and attribute sensitivities unchanged, and zeroing out suppression shifts the posterior mean WTP for a romantic companion by +$1.62/month, independently corroborating the conjoint-based welfare correction."

title: Energy Security in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis Using a Two-Stage Principal Component Approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: Energy security is a critical development challenge in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) amid industrialization, universal electricity access, and the pursuit of a just energy transition. This study develops a composite Energy Security Index for 27 SSA countries over 2005–2023 using a two-stage principal component analysis (PCA). Five dimensions—system adequacy, access and affordability, external vulnerability, environmental sustainability, and institutional conditions—are first reduced through PCA and then combined into a normalized 0–1 composite index. Results reveal substantial disparities: South Africa and Mauritius consistently rank highest, while the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, and Mozambique remain among the least secure. Ethiopia, Rwanda, Togo, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Uganda record the largest improvements, whereas South Africa, Namibia, and Mauritius experience modest declines. Environmental sustainability is negatively correlated with the other dimensions (-0.21 to -0.69), highlighting a trade-off between energy security and sustainability. The findings underscore the need for differentiated Just Energy Transition strategies across structurally diverse SSA economies.

detail.abstract: India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) now handles billions of payments each month, yet little is known about how its effortlessness shapes the everyday spending habits of young users. Drawing on behavioural research on the "pain of paying" and on recent Indian studies linking UPI to impulse buying, this pilot study asked how a small group of mostly young UPI users describe their payment habits, their awareness of their own spending, and the situations in which they make unplanned purchases. An online questionnaire was completed by 27 respondents (aged 16-47; median age 17), recruited by convenience sampling. Results are descriptive. Over half (52%) used UPI daily or more often, and 89% used it for payments of ₹100 or less. Only 15% said they knew their weekly UPI spending accurately. Hunger was the most commonly cited trigger of unplanned purchases (57% of those who reported making them), followed by seeing something while scrolling (29%), and 52% said UPI makes them spend more or more often. Contrary to what the pain-of-paying literature would predict, respondents who chose a payment mode were more likely to say they would hesitate to spend ₹300 online (70%) than in cash (30%), although this difference was not statistically distinguishable from an even split. Willingness to order a meal rose from 48% to 93% when the same menu was shown with a ₹120 discount, but because the discounted option also carried a lower final price, this cannot be attributed to framing. Given the small, non-random sample, the findings are indicative only and are offered as hypotheses for larger studies.

detail.abstract: Financial-news datasets often expose source or publisher counts as measures of attention breadth, but nominal source richness need not equal distinct information supply. We evaluate that measurement problem in a historical Tiingo News sample covering 35 high-support equities from February through September 2026. Using a semantic transform fitted exclusively on pre-period headlines, we represent each publication surface by its within-firm-day TF-IDF centroid and measure cross-surface similarity without using market outcomes. Median raw publication-surface breadth is 8.00 and median mean cross-surface cosine similarity is 0.0395. An intuitive linear semantic-breadth adjustment retains most raw breadth (median 7.70), while a q=2 Leinster-Cobbold effective-number measure yields a median of 5.92. Under article-volume weighting, median q=2 effective diversity is 2.96 and is only moderately rank-correlated with publisher-balanced diversity (Spearman rho=0.594). These are distinct estimands rather than sequential corrections of raw breadth. Direct exact/near headline reuse is sparse on the typical entity-day (median hard matched coverage 0.66%) but strongly associated with continuous semantic redundancy (Spearman rho=0.742). A prespecified blinded 300-pair human audit provides partial external construct support: cosine medians increase across human similarity categories and substantially-same versus different-topic discrimination reaches AUC 0.817, but ordinal-label/cosine Spearman is 0.277 and the same-event categories are sparse. Publication-surface richness, abundance balance, and semantic distinctness are therefore related but non-equivalent properties of financial information supply.

title: Shared Knowledge Model and Shared Awareness Model for Innovation Through Dual Pathway
affiliations: University of Leeds

detail.title: Shared Knowledge Model and Shared Awareness Model for Innovation Through Dual Pathway

detail.abstract: Shared mental models are central to team cognition yet paradoxical for innovation: shared understanding enables coordination but may constrain novelty. Integrating situationawareness research from human factors with research on collective attention, mindfulness, and sensemaking, we distinguish a Shared Awareness Model (SAM), where cues are collectively noticed yet interpretively open, from a Shared Knowledge Model (SKM), where information is collectively elaborated, integrated, and action-guiding. SAM primarily supports exploration, error surfacing, and idea generation; SKM supports evaluation, coordination, and implementation. Their characteristic risks are indeterminacy and premature closure, respectively, and each can compensate for the other. Collective elaboration converts awareness into knowledge, whereas novelty, discrepancy, and deliberate questioning reopen awareness. Generative AI may accelerate the former while narrowing the latter. Innovation thus depends on what teams share and how they move between awareness and knowledge. We also offer a research agenda for testing these propositions.

title: Fiscal Constraints and Information Value in Education Policy

detail.abstract: Fiscal restrictions can limit the value of learning productive education returns. In an education economy with endogenous fertility and partially identified returns, we characterize when minimax regret reaches its information floor at a positive observation error. Under supporting-policy attainment and uniform curvature bounds, saturation occurs exactly when the welfare deficit from restricted authority is maximized only at endpoints and decreases strictly into the return interval. An admitted binding education-price ceiling satisfies this criterion at every known finite elasticity of substitution above one, whereas a binding wage-tax ceiling creates a constant deficit and leaves information value unchanged across menus. Additional curvature conditions establish all-precision minimax complementarity. Under Bayesian evaluation, a strictly convex deficit orders information values across menus, while strictly convex informed values preserve a positive gain from exact revelation whenever posterior uncertainty remains.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the early diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) is visible in productivity and price outcomes relevant to monetary policy. We combine firm-level information on AI adoption from Korea's Survey of Business Activities with annual industry-and region-level data for 2017-2023. We construct value-added-and employment-weighted measures of AI intensity and use their 2019 values as predetermined measures of initial AI intensity. Both measures strongly predict the cross-sectional distribution of AI intensity in 2023. We then estimate reduced-form panel regressions that compare 2023 outcomes across industries and regions with different initial levels of AI intensity, controlling for unit and year fixed effects. We find no systematic evidence that more AI-intensive industries or regions experienced stronger output or labour-productivity growth in 2023. Industry-level price effects are also statistically insignificant and vary across price measures. At the regional level, however, employment-weighted AI intensity is positively associated with overall consumer price inflation, while restaurant price inflation is higher under both measures of AI intensity. These findings suggest that the supply-side benefits of AI had not yet become visible in aggregate productivity by 2023, whereas inflationary pressures may have emerged in some locally determined consumer services. This pattern is consistent with demand responding before productivity gains are fully realised, although our empirical design does not identify the underlying mechanism. The findings have important implications for monetary policy: during the early stages of AI diffusion, central banks should not assume that anticipated productivity gains will immediately expand effective supply or alleviate inflationary pressures. We discuss the implications of this transitional asymmetry for central banks in Asian economies, where rapid AI adoption may coincide with persistent supply constraints and sector-specific price pressures.

detail.abstract: We study the value of optimally designed information under local differential privacy in a Bayesian decision problem. With finitely many types and a full-support prior, feasible posteriors form a compact polytope. For positive privacy parameters, we characterize its extreme points by their two-level likelihood ratios relative to the prior and use this characterization to reduce welfare maximization to a finite linear program. Near full privacy, we derive an exact first-order expansion of optimal welfare. The coefficient is positive if and only if two actions optimal at the prior have distinct payoff vectors; otherwise, with finitely many actions, even optimally designed information cannot improve welfare under sufficiently strong privacy. Near full information, we establish an exact asymptotic expansion of welfare loss and characterize its leading coefficient as the minimum cost of a weighted covering by groups of types sharing an optimal action under full information. The coefficient is positive if and only if no action is optimal for every type; a smaller positive coefficient allows the same sufficiently small welfare shortfall to be attained with stronger privacy protection. Over a range of finite privacy parameters, overlapping designs can outperform every two-level partition mechanism even when each type has a unique preferred recommendation.

title: Neotocracy as a New Academic Discipline and Civilizational Alternative to Capitalism and Communism: Conceptual Foundations of the Model

detail.abstract: Contemporary socioeconomic governance suffers from a structural breakdown born of a false dichotomy. Both market capitalism and state-directed socialism rely on an identical extractive mechanism: the systematic alienation of value from the direct producer via parasitic intermediariesbe they speculative equity holders or bureaucratic apparatchiks. This paper establishes the theoretical foundations of Neotocracy, a novel academic discipline and civilizational paradigm engineered to bypass both private rent-seeking and state coercion. By integrating New Institutional Economics, Systems Dynamics, and deterministic protocol verification, Neotocracy models an autonomous, nonparasitic architecture for resource allocation and institutional governance. Value is anchored to immutable physical and thermodynamic constants rather than inflationary fiat representation, while production is organized through self-governing, highly specialized productive cells operating without external equity extraction. Social security, public goods, and scientific infrastructure are disintermediated, funded automatically via transparent, protocol-level reserves embedded in transactional flows. Neotocracy offers a mathematically grounded framework that renders both central planning and financial extraction obsolete. Sovereignty surrenders to software.

title: Psychogenics: Paradigm Shift from Hermeneutic Psychology to Neural Architecture Engineering

detail.abstract: Contemporary psychological practice remains structurally tethered to a nineteenth-century hermeneutic paradigm that prioritizes verbal introspection, retrospective narrative construction, and subjective interpretation over objective neurobiological metrics. This paper formalizes Psychogenics-a new academic discipline and engineering framework designed to supersede classical psychological models. By integrating predictive coding algorithms, real-time biomarker profiling, epigenomic modulation, and autonomic nervous system regulation, Psychogenics redefines human consciousness as an emergent, open-system architecture rather than an isolated Cartesian interiority. We demonstrate the methodological bankruptcy of traditional conversational therapies in conditions of high informational entropy, outline the quantitative mechanics of the bio-psycho-techno-social interface, and establish a rigorous operational framework for direct neural state optimization. The persistence of conversational diagnostics in an era dominated by molecular biology, neuroimaging, and computational psychiatry represents a profound epistemological failure. Traditional therapeutic modalities operate on the flawed assumption that symbolic manipulation within the prefrontal cortex can directly rewrite entrenched subcortical patterns, un-mesh chronic autonomic hyper-arousal, or reverse the neurotoxic cascades induced by chronic allostatic load. Psychogenics dismantles this linguistic fallacy. It replaces the speculative archeology of childhood memory with precise, real-time monitoring of inflammatory cytokines, heart rate variability, neurotransmitter precursors, and neural network connectivity. Rather than treating subjective distress as an abstract existential puzzle requiring endless verbal decoding, Psychogenics conceptualizes psychological dysfunction as a measurable, engineering-level failure of system homeostasis and information processing. This manuscript details the core operational architecture of Psychogenics across ten distinct theoretical chapters. We establish how predictive coding mechanisms govern the generation of perceptual bias, how chromatin remodeling invalidates the dogma of early-childhood trauma determinism, and how targeted autonomic intervention bypasses the cognitive limitations of the talking cure. By shifting the clinical paradigm from retrospective narrative building to active, closedloop neural state modification, Psychogenics provides the theoretical and practical scaffolding required for genuine human self-design in high-entropy technological environments.

title: Teaching Macroeconomic Dynamics: Analyzing the Carlin-Soskice Three-Equation Macro Model Using MATLAB and the Routh-Hurwitz Criterion

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel pedagogical and methodological framework defined by four key departures from the standard Three-Equation macroeconomic model established by Carlin and Soskice (2005). First, unlike the traditional framework, this approach targets applied mathematics students to bridge economic intuition and formal dynamical systems theory. Second, rather than relying on discrete-time setups or purely conceptual diagrams, the model is formalized using continuous-time differential equations, leveraging the Jacobian matrix for localized stability analysis alongside geometric phase diagrams for qualitative interpretation. Third, to rigorously assess the behavior of higher-dimensional dynamics without sacrificing analytical depth, the Routh-Hurwitz criterion is incorporated to evaluate stability within the resulting 3 × 3 continuous-time system. Finally, the focus shifts from static equilibrium points to dynamic computational exploration by emphasizing parameter sweeps empowering students to map and visualize complex regime shifts across the model's parameter space. To support this quantitative framework, all mathematical computations, stability assessments, and parameter visualizations are executed using MATLAB.

title: On Haavelmo's Adoption of Neyman-Pearson theory

detail.title: On Haavelmo's Adoption of Neyman-Pearson theory

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no conflicts of interest

detail.abstract: Haavelmo's (1944) monograph "The Probability Approach in Econometrics" constitutes the probabilistic foundation for modern econometrics. It is based on a strict adoption of Neyman-Pearson (NP) testing theory in which probability is defined as a long-run relative frequency, and where statistical inference is thought of as deductive reasoning with focus on long-run error control in repeated applications. NP theory does not accomodate inductive probabilistic inference from a unique set of data to an underlying population or theory model, which is precisely the main aim of Haavelmo. Thus, I argue that Haavelmo's adoption of NP theory is inconsistent. In his attempt to make frequentist hypothesis testing fit his purpose, Haavelmo resorted to the notion of a hypothetical infinite population and a distinctly non-frequentist (Bayesian-like) interpretation of probability, in direct contradiction with NP theory. I also discuss the legacy of Haavelmo's probability approach and how it has permeated econometric theory and practice.

title: Syncretics: The Methodological Unification of Cognitive Stratification and the Abolition of Disciplinary Enclosure

detail.abstract: Contemporary educational and epistemological apparatus operates as an industrial mechanism engineered to manufacture cognitive invalids through disciplined fragmentation. By partitioning human consciousness into hermetically sealed professional silos, the modern university enforces an intellectual enclosure that subordinates inquiry to bureaucratic utility and specialized docility. I coin, formulate, and establish the theoretical foundations of Universonomics as a comprehensive civilizational architecture, alongside Syncretics-an emergent methodological discipline and operational core designed to anchor this macro-system. This framework dismantles traditional taxonomic boundaries by establishing structural isomorphism across radical conceptual domains. Rejecting superficial compromises of conventional interdisciplinarity, Syncretics provides a rigorous architecture for the synchronized mastery of political economy, biophysics, and material production. By examining structural functionalism of autonomous agents against systemic fragility of hyper-specialized bureaucrats, this study establishes that true civilizational resilience requires the systematic elimination of the capitalist division of mental and manual labor. Consequently, Syncretics offers an essential diagnostic framework for overcoming cognitive enclosure, restoring human agency, and constructing self-sustaining socio-ecological systems capable of withstanding planetary-scale institutional collapse.

detail.title: A Biosphere-Immersive View of Accounting and Accountability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no conflict of interests.
declarations.funderStatement: the ADVANCE Research Centre at ISEG, and the Portuguese national funding agency for science, research and technology (FCT - Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia, I.P.), under Project UIDB/04521/2020

detail.abstract: Accounting and accountability are activities that have consequences for the relationship between human societies and the biosphere. This article argues that a biosphere-immersive view of accounting and accountability offers an alternative to the mainstream accounting and economic views, as well as the poststructuralist/postmodernist view and a recent definition of accounting. The definition of accounting must incorporate important findings from ecological and green accountability research. Furthermore, it must deconstruct the overreaching influence of economics and the metaphysical status of money, where monetary flows are treated as the constitutive beings (ousia) of economic and societal activity. In the empirical status of money, monetary flows have no explanatory privilege over other flows connected to the biosphere. Accounting and accountability result in biosphere-immersive activities because they attend to how humans are related to their surrounding environment and other living beings. Accounting has ecological implications that must be considered in accounting research. A biosphere-immersive view of accounting and accountability can enhance socioecological perspectives. It can also help find theoretical alternatives to the dominant economic theory in mainstream accounting and economics and the relativism inherent to the poststructuralist/postmodernist research program.

title: Urban Scale, Intra-Urban Spatial Position, and Organizational Performance in the NBA
affiliations: VinUniversity

detail.title: Urban Scale, Intra-Urban Spatial Position, and Organizational Performance in the NBA

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests related to this working paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding from any public, commercial, or nonprofit funding agency.

detail.abstract: Metropolitan scale and location within a city may influence how organizations convert financial resources into performance. This study examines these relationships using National Basketball Association team–season data for 31 team-market units over the seasons labeled 2000–2024. Metropolitan population represents urban scale, while arena distance from the central business district captures one dimension of intra-urban spatial position. The empirical design distinguishes regular-season wins per inflation-adjusted payroll dollar from ordered postseason advancement. A team-market and year fixed-effects model evaluates nonlinear population and distance associations with payroll efficiency. Ordered probit specifications examine postseason advancement, the interaction between arena distance and the league-wide salary cap, and payroll relative to the cap. Across the three models, population exhibits a convex association with performance, with estimated minima of approximately 4.55–6.9 million residents. Payroll efficiency also exhibits a convex association with transformed arena distance. In the postseason models, payroll is positively associated with advancement, and the negative distance–cap interaction indicates that the latent-index slope on distance declines as the cap rises. These findings connect metropolitan scale and intra-urban spatial position to organizational performance within a common institutional setting.

title: Constitutional Authority, Separation of Powers and Institutional Legitimacy: Contestability as a Condition of Constitutionalism, Democracy and the Rule of Law

detail.abstract: Constitutional democracies justify the authority of their institutions by appeal to at least three principles that do not always point in the same direction: democratic pedigree, legal form, and the limitation of power. Scholarship has tended to resolve the tension by selecting one institution as the privileged bearer of legitimacy, whether the elected legislature, the constitutional court, or the executive that claims a direct popular mandate. This article asks whether a more reliable criterion of institutional legitimacy can be derived from the structure of separation of powers itself. Using doctrinal and comparative legal analysis of constitutional texts and apex-court and supranational decisions in the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, Brazil and the European Union, together with institutional analysis of recent episodes of constitutional erosion, the article develops a contestability condition. On this argument, the exercise of constitutional authority is legitimate to the extent that it is allocated according to differentiated institutional competence, remains answerable to an institution with independent standing to contest it, and produces reasoned outcomes that stay open to revision. The article argues that this condition applies symmetrically to legislatures, executives and courts, including constitutional courts, and that contemporary erosion typically proceeds by disabling independent contestation while preserving formal institutional appearances. It confronts the strongest objections from political constitutionalism and from the finality of adjudication, identifies conditions under which the thesis would fail, and draws limited implications for judicial review of structural questions, appointment and removal safeguards, and the accountability of apex courts. The contribution is interpretive and normative rather than empirical, and it is offered as a refinement of existing theories rather than a replacement for them. The author critically reviewed, edited, verified, and assumed responsibility for all legal analysis, argumentation, sources, interpretations, data, and conclusions contained in the final manuscript.

detail.abstract: Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall measure how much a portfolio can lose, not which events accompany its losses. We define News at Risk (NaR): the composition of portfolio tail days over event states, by count and by loss. An identity links each state's share of breaches to its base rate and its lift, its breach rate relative to an average day. Reweighting or deleting event states in historical losses expresses this composition in loss units. We apply the framework to US payroll releases and scheduled Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decisions, 1994-2026, on an equity index, two Treasury yield exposures and a 60/40 book. Composition differs across portfolios. Payroll days are 4.8% of the calendar but 14.8% of the 10-year exposure's 95% breaches, a lift of 3.11 against 1.36 for equities. The 60/40 book has its own composition, not an average of its legs, and for a long euro position FOMC days carry a 99% lift of 6.39. Composition also depends on the risk model: a calendar adjustment fitted on 1994-2018 lowers the 10-year payroll lift on 2019-2026 from 2.85 to 1.10, while a GARCH(1,1) threshold leaves it at 3.44, so a high lift can flag predictable announcement risk that the risk model omits. Splitting payroll days by surprise reverses the dangerous sign across books: beats for rates, misses for equities. All results are descriptive associations.

detail.abstract: Fiscal restrictions shape who gains from correcting education competition and whether a best permanent policy exists. We study endogenous fertility under an education-tax ceiling and nonnegative child transfers. Reoptimizing policy to give greater weight to future cohorts can lower current-parent welfare while benefiting later cohorts even with zero intergenerational transmission. In a constructed example, a cohort weight of 0.1 yields consumption-equivalent changes of-0.53 percent for current parents and 10.01 percent for the next cohort; lower education elasticities preserve the signs and reduce the magnitudes. Weak competition and the transfer floor ensure a finite allocation optimum, yet unknown equilibrium selection can leave the best policy guarantee unattained. A global characterization for every known finite elasticity of substitution above one shows that this failure persists locally but changes across elasticities. For increasing concave bounded education returns, we also derive a resource-optimal education-tax threshold independent of the return function's shape. Fiscal bounds can nevertheless prevent implementation. The results connect intergenerational incidence to the conditions admitting corrective policy.

detail.abstract: We study the impact of school disruptions on children's developmental outcomes, exploiting Covid-19-induced school closures as an exogenous shock to early childhood education. Using population-wide Australian school census data on children in their first year of formal schooling and a difference-indifferences (DID) design, we find that school disruptions negatively affect developmental outcomes. We further examine the role of parental input using a difference-indifference in differences (DDD) framework. We find that the adverse effects of school closures are larger for children from low-resource families, widening developmental inequalities across socioeconomic groups. To explore underlying mechanisms, we investigate parents' behavioural and mental health responses to school closures. Parents in areas with more intensive school closures spent more time with their children, suggesting that parental input partly substitutes for school-based learning. However, they were less likely to engage in high-return educational activities. While low-resource parents increased time investments more than high-resource parents, they remained substantially less likely to undertake high-return educational activities. Our findings highlight the limits of parental input as a substitute for formal schooling and suggest that policies supporting effective home-based learning may be more effective than income support alone in mitigating the adverse effects of future school disruptions.

title: The Unbearable Lightness of Data Portability: Three Lineages yet No Core
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania Law School

detail.title: The Unbearable Lightness of Data Portability: Three Lineages yet No Core

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

affiliations.org_name: University of Pennsylvania - Faculty of Law

detail.abstract: Data portability-the ability of users to access and transfer their personal data between digital services-has become a central feature of privacy and competition policy, appearing in the GDPR, the Digital Markets Act, state privacy statutes such as California's CCPA and CPRA, and sector-specific regimes such as the CFPB's open-banking rule. This Article argues that portability became attractive because it absorbed an older ideal of open systems, and that it turned unstable once that ideal was translated into law and asked to serve privacy, autonomy, interoperability, and competition at once. Three lineages converged on the word: a privacy and access lineage grounded in the European right to informational self-determination; a sector-specific serviceportability lineage exemplified by telephone number portability, HIPAA, and open banking; and an opensystems lineage carrying the echo of the mantra that information wants to be free. That third lineage is the least examined. Its history has been recovered but never carried forward into the law it shaped. Contemporary regimes inherit all three without deciding which controls, producing uncertain scope, security tradeoffs, and weak or distorted competitive effects. The Article can press that claim because the evidence has finally arrived. Enough time has passed since Article 20 and the UK's open-banking regime took effect that a substantial empirical literature now exists, and this Article offers the first comprehensive account of it: audits of what portability requests actually return, studies measuring entry and its distributional consequences, and formal models identifying when portability raises or lowers welfare. That record bears out the lessons of earlier efforts, from number portability to interconnection-cream-skimming, a persistent need for regulatory micromanagement, and entry at strategic margins rather than against incumbents. The Article closes with a limiting principle: portability mandates are most defensible where the data is standardized, operational, and tightly connected to interoperability, and least defensible where they make broad categories of user-generated content portable in the hope that access alone will answer structural competition concerns.

detail.abstract: Solid waste management remains a critical environmental and public health challenge in high-density suburbs across sub-Saharan Africa. This study investigated household waste disposal practices and associated factors in Makokoba, a high-density suburb of Bulawayo, Zimbabwe. A cross-sectional quantitative design was employed, involving 173 households selected through stratified systematic random sampling. Data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires administered through face-to-face interviews. The primary outcome was illegal waste disposal, defined as any method other than municipal collection services. Curbside collection was the most used method, though it was utilised by fewer than 50% of respondents. The rest of the respondents reported burning, burying and open dumping as their regular waste disposal method. Chi-square analysis revealed that only the presence of a designated disposal point was significantly associated with proper waste disposal practices (χ² = 4.25, p = 0.039). A Firth logistic regression model identified the presence of a designated disposal point as the only significant predictor of proper waste disposal (OR = 1.86; 95% CI: 1.02-3.40; p = 0.042). Respondents identified infrastructure deficits and social factors as key challenges affecting waste management. They proposed infrastructure improvements (52%), awareness programmes (18%), and policy changes (17%) as solutions. The findings show the importance of infrastructure accessibility over knowledge and attitudes in shaping waste disposal behaviour. To reduce illegal waste disposal, interventions should prioritise the provision of accessible disposal facilities and reliable collection services.

title: Not All That's Abandoned Is Lost: The Informational Role of Withdrawn Patent Applications
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics, Capital University of Economics and Business and Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: Not All That's Abandoned Is Lost: The Informational Role of Withdrawn Patent Applications

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors have no conflict of interest with others
declarations.funderStatement: NA

affiliations.org_name: Central University of Finance and Economics
Capital University of Economics and Business

detail.abstract: It remains an open question whether withdrawn patent applications are worthless or retain any informational value. Utilizing a unique dataset from China, we find that patent examiners tend to use withdrawn applications as prior art to reject subsequent patent filings by other firms. This effect is more pronounced when the withdrawing firms are leaders in patent races, when the signaling content of the withdrawal behavior is more substantial, when competition in both the patent class and product markets is more intense, and when innovation uncertainty within the patent class is higher. Using Office Action data, our channel tests show that examiners are more likely to issue rejection decisions after encountering a patent withdrawal during examination; furthermore, when an Office Action cites a withdrawn patent, the probability of rejection for the patent under examination increases. Further analysis shows that firms that withdraw patent applications tend to achieve greater success in their subsequent patent applications. However, other firms within the same technological domain appear unable to learn from the information embedded in withdrawn applications. Overall, our findings shed light on the informational value of abandoned patents in the patent examination process and their broader role in shaping the innovation environment.

detail.abstract: The campaign against sex trafficking in Victorian and Edwardian England was not simply a humanitarian response to the exploitation of women and girls. It was also connected to wider debates about morality, national identity, masculinity, imperial respectability, gender relations and the responsibilities of the British state. During the second half of the nineteenth century and the opening years of the twentieth century, reformers increasingly drew public attention to the movement of women and girls into prostitution through deception, coercion and economic vulnerability. In contemporary language, this phenomenon was frequently described as the "white slave trade." The expression carried racial and national assumptions that are important for understanding the period. It presented the exploitation of white European women as a form of slavery and often connected their protection to the moral reputation of Britain. This article examines the relationship between patriotism, masculinity and anti-trafficking activism in Victorian and Edwardian England. It focuses particularly on the National Vigilance Association (NVA), established in 1885, and its later international work through the International Bureau for the Suppression of the White Slave Traffic. It also considers the earlier campaign against the Contagious Diseases Acts and the contribution of figures such as Josephine Butler and William Thomas Stead. The study argues that male reformers often presented the protection of women and girls as a masculine responsibility, while national rhetoric transformed the protection of English womanhood into a matter of British honour and social order. At the same time, the anti-trafficking movement was not internally consistent. Some activists challenged the sexual double standard and demanded greater protection for women, while others promoted restrictive ideas about female sexuality, immigration and respectable behaviour. The movement could therefore challenge exploitation while simultaneously reproducing assumptions about class, race and gender. The article concludes that the fight against sex trafficking in Victorian and Edwardian England should be understood as both a reform movement and a product of its historical environment. Its achievements were significant, but its language and methods also reveal the limitations of contemporary ideas about gender, national identity and social purity.

detail.abstract: Recent domestic and international incidents-including fatal industrial accidents, severe climate-driven heat stress on garment workers, and widespread wage and safety violationsunderscore persistent vulnerabilities in global manufacturing and infrastructure. In response to these ongoing challenges and the shifting dynamics of global supply chains, India has overhauled its regulatory framework by consolidating 29 outdated central statutes into four unified labour codes. While these sweeping reforms aim to reduce bureaucratic hurdles, boost operational flexibility to attract foreign investment, and formalize emerging sectors like the gig economy, they have simultaneously drawn sharp criticism from trade unions concerned over potential rollbacks of fundamental worker protections. In this light, this study reviews the impact of new labour codes and talks about its state wise implementation. Moreover, we also focus on GAIL (India) Limited and attempt to find out whether the Maharatna Company is making best use of India's ongoing Labour reforms and the New Labour Codes through streamlined regulatory compliance, as the consolidation of multiple archaic acts into four unified codes reduces administrative overhead and minimizes legal disputes. By adopting standardized definitions like uniform wage structures and clear fixed-term employment guidelines, GAIL can enhance workforce flexibility, operational predictability, and corporate governance. Ultimately, this approach fosters a more harmonious and productive industrial relations environment across its energy projects.

detail.abstract: Mental health is a vital at adolescent development. This study aimed to determine the mental well-being of senior high school learners in terms of depression, anxiety, and stress; identify the perceived causes of these conditions in terms of academic, personal, lifestyle, social, and financial; and propose a contextualized mental health initiative based on the findings. The study utilized a descriptive research design involving 330 senior high school learners at Victoria National High School, Victoria, Tarlac, selected through stratified random sampling. Data was gathered using the standardized Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21) and a researchermade questionnaire on the causes of depression, anxiety, and stress. Frequency counts, percentages, weighted mean, and descriptive statistics were used in analyzing the data. Findings revealed that most respondents had normal levels of depression and normal levels of stress. However, anxiety is the most prominent concern, with the majority of respondents classified under moderate anxiety and severe anxiety. Furthermore, all identified causes were perceived as significant causes of depression, anxiety, and stress. Among these, academics ranked highest, followed by lifestyle, financial, personal, and social. These results indicate that learners' mental health concerns are influenced by both school-related and personal life circumstances. Based on the findings, a contextualized mental health initiative entitled KALMADO (Kaagapay sa Alagang Lakas-Mental at Damdamin ng mga Estudyante) was proposed. The initiative includes programs on academic support, personal wellness, healthy lifestyle promotion, peer support, and financial guidance. It is recommended that schools implement initiatives to support the mental well-being of the learners.

title: Does Corporate Governance Protect Firms in Market Crises? Point-in-Time Evidence from Borsa Istanbul's 2018 Currency Crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 Crash

detail.abstract: Do firms with stronger corporate governance lose less in market crises? I study Borsa Istanbul's 2018 currency crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 crash, using membership in the BIST Corporate Governance Index (XKURY) at the start of each episode, which I reconstruct from the dates of governance-rating announcements instead of applying today's index list. The samples contain 267–270 non-financial firms per episode, of which 26–27 are index members. Members' raw maximum drawdown is 2.0 percentage points (pp) smaller than other firms' in 2018 (p = 0.33) and 7.0 pp smaller in 2020 (p = 0.005). Members are also roughly 12–14 times larger and trade less intensively. With controls for size, trading intensity and pre-crisis beta, the estimated membership coefficient lies between −0.6 and +0.6 pp in 2018 and between +3.7 and +4.2 pp in 2020 (p = 0.08–0.15). Size accounts for all of the 2018 raw difference and about half of the 2020 difference. In a common-support sample of larger firms, the 2020 estimates fall to between +1.4 and +2.2 pp and the 2018 estimates turn negative. Drawdowns relative to the market, matching estimators and rating scores within the member group show no reliable association either. In 2018, however, members underperformed the equal-weighted market by 8–11 pp in buy-and-hold abnormal returns, an exploratory result that does not appear in 2020. Members were less likely to regain their market-relative price peak (unconditionally significant only in 2020), but the difference is not significant once size and beta are controlled. The 95% confidence intervals reach about +5 pp in 2018, +9 pp in 2020 and +5.5 pp in a pooled panel, so the evidence is inconclusive: it cannot exclude small protective effects, and in 2020 it cannot exclude larger ones. Using today's index membership would misclassify about a third of the apparent members, although here it changes the maximumdrawdown estimates only modestly. A price-jump filter has to allow for Borsa Istanbul's changing daily price limits.

detail.abstract: Procurement can reduce government spending but limit consumer access to preferred products. We study this trade-off in China’s Volume-Based Procurement, which prioritizes winners in hospitals but not pharmacies. Using calcium channel blockers, we show consumers shift toward non-procured drugs. Although hospital price decreases, 82% of the decline comes from substitution toward cheaper products. Combining both channels, our structural model shows that price-only procurement selects lower-cost products with lower perceived quality. Relative to no program, Volume-Based Procurement saves 30-billion RMB reimbursement but lowers consumer surplus by 12-billion RMB. Quality-adjusted scoring rule recovers 76% of this loss with reimbursements rising only 13.5%.

title: Order-Four Ordinal Patterns of Time-Changed Brownian Motion: Equal-Lag Detection of Reversible Volatility Clocks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Order-Four Ordinal Patterns of Time-Changed Brownian Motion: Equal-Lag Detection of Reversible Volatility Clocks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded.

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract:
The equal-lag order-3 ordinal statistics of a time-changed Brownian motion are exactly blind to every reversible independent volatility clock, so that clock detection there requires unequal lags (Adibi, 2026). We show that this blindness does not persist at order four. All twenty-four order-4 pattern probabilities of a time-changed Brownian motion with an independent clock admit an exact conditional representation as centred trivariate Gaussian orthant probabilities, a sum of three arcsines of the clock-increment correlations. Under a reversible independent clock the available symmetry is the Klein four-group generated by the global sign flip and time reversal. Its action partitions the patterns into eight orbits, equal within themselves but, unlike the order-3 turning patterns, not all pinned to their Brownian values. Two orbits, carrying exactly half the probability mass, remain blind to every stationary reversible clock; each of the other six moves under some such clock, subject to three exact linear relations, and all six move under the multifractal clock. For the lognormal multifractal random measure we prove a closed-form equal-lag deviation,

 p_σ^MRW − p_σ^BM = λ²δ_σ + O(λ⁴), D₄ := δ₁₃₄₂ = (√2/128π) log(16/243), 

the coefficient of largest magnitude, with every orbit coefficient elementary in log 2, log 3 and surds. By exact stochastic scale invariance the deviation is independent of the sampling lag and of the integral scale at every intermittency. The common multifractal drift cancels, the exact opposite of the order-3 mechanism, and the deviation is pure curvature: the Hessian of the orthant probability contracted against the log-clock covariance. Order-4 ordinal patterns therefore detect a reversible multifractal clock at equal lags, a cleaner channel than the order-3 unequal-lag deviation. With optimal contrasts it is about five times cheaper to resolve, whatever the order-3 window ratio, though at plausible intermittencies it remains a high-frequency observable requiring of order 10⁵ patterns. We give a model-free expansion with explicit third-order remainder, sharpened to the rate O(λ⁴), and an estimator-design analysis showing the orbit-count vector is sufficient. We prove the leading-order expansion and equal-lag detection at every pattern order n ≥ 4, identify two closed-form thresholds across pattern order, and evaluate the order-five coefficients from the Plackett reduction, which predict the orbits a direct simulation resolves.

title: An Influence-driven Reaction–advection–Diffusion Model for Spatial Gambling Dynamics: Mathematical Analysis and Application to Khomas Region, Namibia
affiliations: University of Namibia, University of Namibia and University of Namibia

detail.title: An Influence-driven Reaction–advection–Diffusion Model for Spatial Gambling Dynamics: Mathematical Analysis and Application to Khomas Region, Namibia
detail.abstract: Gambling behaviour in Namibia's Khomas Region may be shaped not only by local behavioural transitions but also by spatial heterogeneity in gambling-related influence, including uneven exposure to gambling venues, advertising, accessibility, and socially engaged populations. Existing reaction--diffusion formulations of spatial gambling dynamics capture local behavioural transitions and undirected diffusive redistribution but do notexplicitly represent directed transport associated with spatially varying gambling-related influence. This study extends the reaction--diffusion framework to an influence-driven reaction--advection--diffusion model formulated within a conservation-law framework. A prescribed gambling influence potential $\Phi(x)$ is constructed from aggregate behaviouralobservations and prescribed spatial influence profiles, and its spatial gradient generates an influence-driven advective flux. Positivity, conservation, $L^1$-boundedness, and stability properties of the resulting dynamical system are analysed. The nonlinear system is solved numerically using a Chebyshev spectral collocation method in space combined with animplicit-explicit (IMEX) Euler scheme in time, with the linear diffusion--advection operator treated implicitly and factorised once for efficient reuse at each time step, while the nonlinear reaction terms are treated explicitly. The model uses aggregate behavioural data from theKhomas Region for model specification and investigates the roles of the influence-sensitivity coefficient $\chi$ and the influence-weighting parameter $\eta$ through numerical sensitivity experiments. Numerical results demonstrate spectral convergence in space and first-order accuracy in time, while the parameter experiments indicate that $\chi$ has a stronger effect on influence-driven spatial redistribution than $\eta$, with changes in $\chi$ producing more pronounced spatial redistribution of gambling engagement. A local sensitivity analysis further identifies the engagement-loss and potential-to-engaged transition rates as parameterswith comparatively strong effects on the model response. The results demonstrate how a prescribed spatial gambling-influence field can extend reaction--diffusion gambling models by providing a mathematically explicit mechanism for influence-driven spatial redistribution.

detail.abstract: Most research on artificial intelligence (AI) and labor demand concerns displacement, or the lack of it. This paper looks at the other margin: creation. Using 882 million online job postings from 2021 to mid-2026, this paper identifies 72 million postings tied to a twelve-segment, five-layer taxonomy of the AI Value Chain (AIVC)-physical infrastructure, data, cross-cutting enablers (cloud computing and cybersecurity), AI development, and AI use-and document where this formal labor demand is being created across more than 200 economies. Three facts stand out. First, AIVC demand has surged since late 2024, led by AI use. After falling to 6.7 percent of all online postings in 2024Q1, the AIVC share rose to 11.2 percent in 2026Q2, and AI use and AI development roughly tripled their share of world postings after the release of ChatGPT. Second, these are predominantly good jobs: 87 percent of AIVC postings are in occupations in the top three deciles of the US wage distribution, against 49 percent of all online postings. Third, high-income countries capture these jobs out of proportion to their workforce. They account for 61 percent of AIVC postings but only 17 percent of the world's working-age population, with 13.7 AIVC postings per 1,000 working-age people in 2026H1, against about 2 in middle-income countries and virtually none in low-income countries. Some middle-income countries outperform. Among developing regions, Latin America, South Asia, and East Asia lead. Developing countries capture their largest shares of world postings in data labeling, AI development, and data engineering. GenAI adoption is significantly associated with AIVC job intensity, in total and in every layer of the value chain. This suggests that faster and deeper AI adoption may help countries capture more of these jobs.

detail.abstract: Building on the axiomatic subgroup Gini decomposition of Heikkuri and Schief (2026), we reinterpret risky capital as a population partitioned by industry and derive a within-industry benchmark that depends only on industry weights and marginal Gini risk. Portfolio Gini splits into this benchmark and a signed across-industry residual that combines cross-industry hedging with industry-risk heterogeneity. Reweighting this residual changes both components. We study the component-weighted criterion alongside a convex hedging-only benchmark that isolates dependence shrinkage. Both criteria serve as partition-dependent risk regularizers. In controlled simulations that fix the realized mean, partial reweighting yields statistically detectable but economically small improvements that the hedging-only benchmark nearly matches, indicating that dependence shrinkage drives the effect. Sample-only cross-validation selects full weighting, with no improvement in risk-adjusted performance. The controlled gains identify a dependence-regularization effect.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the implications of global stablecoin adoption for the monetary and financial architecture, with particular emphasis on the euro area. It employs a flow-of-funds framework tracing sectoral and cross-border balance-sheet adjustments as a function of funding sources and reserve asset composition, operationalised through a calibrated three-region model (United States, euro area, rest of the world), embedding alternative stablecoin growth scenarios for USD- and EUR-denominated stablecoins through 2030. The analysis finds that, even under high stablecoin growth assumptions, aggregate effects on the euro area financial system would likely remain manageable. The principal structural effect on banks is the conversion of stable, inexpensive retail deposits into more volatile and costly wholesale funding. Effects on securities markets, while meaningful in terms of demand reallocation toward short-term sovereign instruments, are likewise assessed as manageable. Stablecoin-specific financial stability risks, though real, are not fundamentally novel and are amenable to standard regulatory mitigation tools. Stablecoins are best understood as part of the continuing evolution of monetary architecture, the significance of which will depend on the efficiency gains they ultimately deliver and the adequacy of the regulatory environment. While financial stability and monetary architecture risks appear manageable, other important societal issues, such as their significant use for illicit payments and regulatory arbitrage, deserve more scrutiny.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how state abortion bans following the 2022 Dobbs decision, which eliminated the federal constitutional right to abortion, affected women's medical out-ofpocket (MOOP) expenditures. To the extent that abortion bans lead to increased birth rates and care complications, we would expect to see increased non-premium MOOP spending associated with this care. We would also expect to see increased MOOP spending on insurance premiums to the extent that individuals take up private insurance or switch to more expensive plans or that insurers pass these costs onto beneficiaries. We use 2019-2025 Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement data and difference-indifferences style analyses to examine individual-level MOOP spending on health insurance premiums and non-premium expenditures by women aged 18-44. Our results show that abortion bans are associated with an increase in women's likelihood of paying out-of-pocket for health insurance premiums. We do not find significant effects on non-premium out-of-pocket expenditures, nor do we find effects for men. For women with household income between 138% and 250% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), we find the premium effects associated with an increase in policyholder employersponsored insurance coverage. In contrast, for women with household income above 250% of the FPL, who make up the majority of our sample, we find the premium effects associated with bearing more of the costs of coverage associated with their private insurance. We further see effects predominantly among Black women and Hispanic women associated with increased takeup of private insurance as well as bearing more of the premium costs. Our results are suggestive that post-Dobbs abortion bans led to insurers passing more premium costs to beneficiaries. Our findings shed light on the more far-reaching effects of abortion bans, quantifying the extent to which they pose an economic burden to individuals and families.

detail.abstract:
Background: Food security remains one of the most consequential global challenges, yet evidence on its status, causes and solutions is fragmented across reports and disciplines. Objective: This review integrates the most recent global, regional and national evidence and examines how food security can be made inclusive for people regardless of literacy. Methods: A systematic narrative review with secondary data analysis was conducted using the 2026 editions of The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) and the Global Report on Food Crises (GRFC), the June 2026 Cadre Harmonisé, and peer-reviewed literature from leading journals and publishers.

Results: Global hunger fell for a third consecutive year to about 645 million people (7.8%) in 2025, and moderate or severe food insecurity to about 2.1 billion (25.8%), but about 520 million people are projected to remain hungry in 2030. Africa (about 309 million) now exceeds Asia (about 292 million) in absolute hunger, and 66.6% of Africans cannot afford a healthy diet. About 266 million people in 47 countries and territories faced acute food insecurity in 2025, famine was confirmed in Sudan and Gaza, and Nigeria faces its highest recorded levels (about 35 to 36 million in Phase 3 or worse in the 2026 lean season). Conflict, climate extremes and economic shocks are the principal drivers, compounded by inequality, weak governance, falling funding and eroding data systems.

Conclusions: Solutions cluster in four areas, produce, protect, nourish and enable, and work best when integrated, predictable and inclusive. Information systems designed for literate and non-literate users can strengthen early warning, targeting and accountability. Scenarios to 2050 show that outcomes depend on political and financing choices.

detail.abstract: The Theory of Dynamic Adaptive Warfare (TDAW), originally formulated in Portuguese as the Teoria da Guerra Dinâmica Adaptativa (TGDA), is presented as a Brazilian post-classical theory of war whose documented research trajectory begins with a strategic and legal problem encountered in 2022, develops through a broader engagement with War Theory and Game Theory in 2024, expands across materially different forms of coercion and conflict in 2025 and reaches systematic general formulation in 2026. The theory responds to explanatory fragmentation rather than to the absence of prior strategic thought. Classical and modern theories remain indispensable, yet contemporary conflict increasingly requires force, strategic interdependence, legal constraint, economic coercion, technology, information, legitimacy, thirdparty support and adaptation to be examined within the same changing system. TDAW therefore integrates three intellectual foundations: War Theory, which explains organized coercion, political purpose, friction, geography and the interaction of wills; Game Theory, which explains decision under strategic interdependence, incomplete information, signaling, bargaining, deterrence, repetition and adaptation; and International Law, which is treated not merely as an external standard of judgment but as part of the strategic environment because legal status, sanctions, alliance arrangements, responsibility, legitimacy and institutional reactions can alter costs and available courses of action. These foundations later converge analytically in the forcedecision-norm triad, which is an architectural synthesis rather than the historical genealogy of the theory. It conceptualizes war as a dynamic, adaptive, multidomain and legally conditioned system in which action generates response, feedback modifies subsequent choices, actors learn with unequal effectiveness and strategic pressure may be reinforced, substituted, or migrated across domains when resistance, cost, opportunity, or risk changes. Conditional predictability is developed as a method of disciplined prospective reasoning rather than deterministic forecasting: it organizes intention, capability, vulnerability, opportunity, legal and political cost, escalation risk, adversarial response and adaptive capacity while requiring explicit assumptions and continuous revision. The present article deliberately explains the theoretical architecture without reproducing the complete equations, numerical metrics, scoring procedures, or operational calibration system, which are developed separately in a forthcoming and currently unpublished Volume II of the integral work devoted to intelligence, defense, simulation and operational predictive modeling. The article instead concentrates on intellectual origin, conceptual precision, mechanisms, scope conditions, rival explanations, falsifiability and the research program through which the theory can be tested, criticized and refined.

detail.abstract: The modern scientific paradigm is undergoing a structural shift driven by big data and AI. High-capacity machine-learning algorithms routinely extract non-linear correlations from massive datasets, inverting the classical research pipeline by generating hypotheses faster than empirical science can evaluate them. However, this data-saturated environment severely amplifies the Duhem–Quine thesis—the philosophical principle that core hypotheses cannot be tested in isolation from auxiliary assumptions. In AI workflows, the algorithm itself acts as a high-capacity, opaque auxiliary assumption, creating epistemic deadlocks when separating genuine causal mechanisms from latent environmental confounders, algorithmic shortcuts, or sensor artifacts. This paper proposes shifting Bayesian epistemology from a retrospective diagnostic tool into a prophylactic pre-experimental protocol for managing—rather than resolving—the Duhem–Quine problem. Building upon Bayesian hypothesis generation, we present a four-stage protocol that operationalizes directed acyclic graphs, pre-registered priors, and calibrated Bayes-factor thresholds before data collection or AI unblinding. We specify the mechanics of probabilistic blame routing across network nodes, provide a fully worked numerical example, and show how pre-registered Bayes-factor gates reduce researcher degrees of freedom and make post-hoc threshold manipulation detectable. The protocol does not eliminate underdetermination or prevent p-hacking; it makes auxiliary assumptions explicit and auditable. A complete four-stage worked example (retinal micro- and nanoplastics) is provided in the Supplementary File. Pre-data Bayesian filters can safeguard empirical resources and accelerate robust scientific inference in the age of big data without claiming to resolve the logical problem of underdetermination,

detail.abstract: Three years after the India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) entered into force in May 2022, the official story is one of triumph: bilateral trade is closing in on 100 billion US dollars. This paper looks past the aggregate at the single sector where CEPA was supposed to matter most for Indian workers and exporters, gems and jewellery, and asks a sharper question. detail.abstract: I study how representation on the House Agriculture Committee affects federal farm subsidies using $394 billion in payments to 4.6 million payees from 1995 through 2024. After a district loses Agriculture representation, farm payments fall by 21.5% and paid recipients by 15.2% relative to other districts in the same state. Subsidies also fall when the departing member remains in the House, and the Agriculture response is statistically distinguishable from the response to Appropriations exit. Formula-based payments fall alongside agricultural activity, insured acreage and liability, and small-farm bank lending. Gaining representation produces an initial increase in payments that fades over time. The pattern is consistent with specialized political representation helping sustain an economic constituency even when formal rules limit discretion over how federal support is allocated.

detail.abstract: Demographic aging is a structural transformation that may affect macroeconomic mechanisms ranging from labor supply and saving to productivity and the effectiveness of monetary and fiscal policy. This paper examines its labor-market effects and business-cycle implications through a theoretical and conceptual synthesis of the literature. Its central argument is that aging has no predetermined, onedirectional effect on growth, inflation, or business cycles. Outcomes vary with the relative importance of labor supply, productivity, saving, consumption, technological adaptation, and policy transmission under different conditions. The demographic adaptation gap offers a conceptual lens through which to examine the distance between demographic pressure and economic and institutional adaptive capacity. Olderworker employment, migration, technological adaptation, pension reform, and care policies are imperfect substitutes: gains in one area may create costs in another. For Türkiye, the literature considered does not conclusively establish the direct effects of aging on inflation, the natural rate of interest, monetary policy transmission, or cyclical volatility. The paper's contribution is an integrated analytical framework for examining these macroeconomic mechanisms together under different conditions of institutional and technological adaptation, rather than reducing demographic aging to a single aggregate outcome.

detail.abstract: African traditional knowledge (TK) and genetic resources remain vulnerable to misappropriation despite growing recognition of community rights and access and benefitsharing (ABS) obligations. National registers, defensive databases and compliance certificates improve visibility and prior-art identification, but they are institutionally centralised and struggle to establish provenance, record community consent, monitor subsequent use or trigger benefit-sharing. This article examines whether blockchain can complement these mechanisms by creating tamper-evident records of the provenance, access, authorised use and licensing of TK and genetic resources. It argues that blockchain is not a substitute for intellectual property law, ABS regimes or customary governance, but a legal-technical infrastructure that can strengthen their evidentiary and accountability functions. Drawing on the ARIPO Swakopmund Protocol, the Nagoya Protocol and the 2024 WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge, it evaluates the opportunities and limits of a permissioned consortium ledger and proposes a communitycentred model in which ledger records operate alongside prior informed consent, mutually agreed terms, confidentiality safeguards and competent institutional oversight. It concludes that the value of blockchain lies not in technological immutability but in whether decentralised ledgers can be legally integrated into African systems of community authority, consent and benefit-sharing.

detail.abstract: Bangladesh's reported GDP growth has been questioned because it diverged from several domestic macroeconomic indicators after the mid-2010s. This paper asks whether an independently selected international nighttime-lights benchmark detects the same anomaly and why the answer changes when electricity access is modeled explicitly. Using the 1992-2024 MVNL series and the model-tournament framework developed in Tahsin (2026), Bangladesh is excluded from model development. The temporally coherent M3 total-radiance benchmark implies slower post-2015 GDP-per-capita growth than reported data and a large 2024 level gap; adding electricity access sharply attenuates that discrepancy. The attenuation survives alternative density specifications and common smoothing, while the exact Bangladesh level remains specification-sensitive because the country lies near the edge of international covariate support. The paper therefore treats the result as triangulation rather than a replacement GDP estimate: conditional on independent macroeconomic evidence being informative, rapid expansion of electricity access may have outpaced the conversion of connections into reliable productive use.

detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of trade liberalization on hospital operations, quality, and community access to healthcare. Consistent with the decline in manufacturing employment following trade shocks---and thus a loss of employer-sponsored health insurance among residents in affected communities---we document a reduction in the intake of privately-insured patients at local hospitals. This decline in privately-insured admissions, which typically provide the highest reimbursement rates for hospital services, has a substantial negative impact on hospital finances. Moreover, hospitals in manufacturing-dependent areas are more likely to close or merge with other hospitals and experience a significant decline in quality of care. At the same time, we observe a rise in healthcare insurance premiums in affected areas, indicating that local hospitals raise prices for patient services to improve their financial situations. The effects are more pronounced for hospitals that relied more on private insurance reimbursements and in areas experiencing greater outmigration and firm closure following trade liberalization. Our findings highlight an overlooked effect of trade liberalization---community access to healthcare---and illustrate the extent to which the healthcare system relies on reimbursements from private insurance.

detail.abstract:
This systematic macro-financial surveillance framework is built to monitor global fiscal sustainability and sovereign risk premium repricing across a cross-sectional cohort comprising North America (Canada, United States), Europe (Germany, France, United Kingdom), Asia (Singapore, China, Japan), Latin America (Chile, Mexico, Brazil), and five global benchmark aggregates (Other Advanced Economies excl. G7 & Euro Area, Middle East and Central Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, Emerging Market & Developing Economies, and G7). Each sovereign's baseline Primary Net Lending (+)/Borrowing balance footprint is demarcated through the 50% Highest Density Region (HDR) over the 2001-2025 cycle, isolating their respective fiscal regime anchors and structural funding capacity. 

Fiscal downside tail risks materialise when the primary balance breaches the 50% HDR lower bound of the corridor, signalling that fiscal slippages have expanded beyond the sovereign's empirical baseline footprint. This regime departure activates a sovereign risk premium repricing transmission channel, triggering credit spread expansions and secondary market liquidity squeezes that steepen the long end of the sovereign yield curve. Ultimately, sovereign risk premium repricing elasticity is structurally asymmetric across safe-asset versus high-beta sovereign profiles when downside fiscal tails are tested.
