detail.abstract: Traditional neural Text-to-Speech (TTS) architectures force a trade-off between human editing control and acoustic fidelity. Syntax-dependent markup languages such as SSML suffer from structural fragility, whereas unconstrained end-to-end neural audio generators obscure granular structural editing and induce the Acoustic Parameter-Identity Entanglement Problem-causing voice identity drift, phase discontinuities, and localized artifacts when prosodic parameters are manually adjusted. In this paper, we present an exhaustive, hardware-accelerated speech synthesis framework powered by a serialized multi-track intermediate markup schema. Our pipeline decouples phoneme timing, continuous prosodic contours, and target speaker identities into synchronized, platform-independent tracks. We introduce a dedicated ASIC-implemented Manifold Projection Processor that projects humanedited prosodic inputs onto a regularized Riemannian target speaker identity submanifold (M s) within the latent neural space under a strict Lipschitz continuity constraint bounded by a variance parameter ϵ. This geometric restriction preserves target vocal timber while allowing rich, real-time expression edits. Furthermore, a hardware-aware, VRAM-sensitive partitioning compiler mitigates GPU memory fragmentation and attention-map collapse during parallel processing by enforcing dynamic payload slicing bounded by a 4,500-character ceiling. Experimental evaluations and rigorous differential geometry proofs demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior naturalness (4.68 ± 0.05 MOS) and voice identity preservation (4.61 ± 0.06 MOS) compared to standard flow-matching and diffusion baselines, while reducing localized acoustic artifacts to 0.8%.

detail.abstract: We ask whether borrowers' social preferences may create non-pecuniary repayment incentives (social monitoring). To study this question, we use credit unions as a setting because, unlike banks, they link owner-borrowers through social ties that may generate social monitoring through altruism, social pressure, or both. Comparing lending outcomes at credit unions and banks of similar size, three findings suggest social monitoring is economically meaningful and point to social pressure as the dominant channel. First, credit unions face lower default rates on loans whose defaults are visible to peers (mortgages), but higher default rates on those whose defaults are not visible (credit cards). Second, these differences are strongest at one- and two-branch institutions, where peers' default visibility is highest. Third, mortgage default differences are strongest for professional bonds and  muted for religious bonds, where  altruism is likely strongest. Observable risk or contract terms in borrower-level data cannot account for these results.

detail.abstract: This paper compares equilibrium bidding strategies in a first-price sealed-bid auction with two asymmetric bidders who have dependent private valuations. Modeling bidder strength via a stochastic asymmetry condition – where one bidder is systematically more likely to hold the maximum valuation – I show that the globally weak bidder, facing a competitive disadvantage at all top valuation levels, bids more aggressively at every valuation. Conversely, the stronger bidder wins more frequently, generalizing Maskin and Riley (2000) to dependent private-value environments. When the stochastic asymmetry flips once, so that each bidder is stronger over a different range, the bid distributions cross once, with each bidder bidding more aggressively where their competitive disadvantage is most acute. In both environments, allocative inefficiency is an inherent feature of the equilibrium, driven by the stronger bidder's heightened incentives to shade bids relative to their valuation. The results translate to procurement auctions and wage competition between employers, and extend to interdependent-value auctions and the war of attrition under modified conditions.

detail.abstract: Exchange-rate movements create financial exposure for Hajj cost management because a substantial share of Hajj-related expenditure is denominated in Saudi riyal. This study quantifies the exposure of Indonesia's Hajj pilgrimage cost (BPIH) to movements in the SAR/IDR exchange rate. Using 29 annual observations covering 1996-2019 and 2022-2026, the study estimates a log-log regression of BPIH on the SAR/IDR exchange rate, controlling for Saudi consumer prices, Brent crude oil prices, and the Hajj quota for Indonesia. The results show a positive relationship between the SAR/IDR exchange rate and BPIH, with an estimated conditional historical elasticity of approximately 0.77. The coefficient remains stable when Brent oil prices are excluded from the model. The estimate indicates that a 10% increase in SAR/IDR is associated with an approximately 7.62% increase in BPIH, ceteris paribus. By quantifying the magnitude of this exposure, the study provides an empirical basis for assessing how currency movements may affect Hajj costs and for incorporating exchange-rate scenarios into Hajj fund risk management.

detail.abstract: Philippine cooperatives exist to serve their members, and cooperative law limits their credit services accordingly. This essay examines Ligas Kooperatiba ng Bayan sa Pagpapaunlad (LKBP), a community cooperative founded by small farmers and businessmen in Barangay Ligas, Malolos, Bulacan, which appears in the audited statements of Breakthrough and Milestones Productions International (BMPI) as the lender behind a construction loan that stood at ₱1.29 billion in 2022 and ₱1.86 billion by the end of 2025. BMPI, the content provider of UNTV, is owned entirely by leaders, relatives, ministers, and officers of the Members Church of God International (MCGI). The loan financed a sixteen-storey tower on EDSA that broke ground in June 2014 as the UNTV Broadcast Center or UNTV Tower and later renamed The Millenial Tower, missed its 2018 target, and remains under construction twelve years later, now rebranded as The Philippine Broadcast Hub. The new name drops UNTV and presents the building as a general broadcast facility; if the tower is let commercially, it would depart from the purposes under which it was financed and presented. Comparing BMPI's 2022 audited statements with LKBP's own annual reports for 2016 to 2025, the essay finds that the two records cannot both be accurate as stated. The balance BMPI reports would equal between 79 and 86 percent of LKBP's entire loan portfolio in 2021 and 2022, and by 2024 and 2025 it exceeded that portfolio outright, and interest at the stated 14 percent would nearly equal all the interest income LKBP earned from its 15,947 members. LKBP's reports never disclose the loan, yet they record a recurring relationship with UNTV, BMPI, and MCGI's charitable foundations. The essay argues that cooperative regulation's reliance on each cooperative's own aggregated reporting, without reconciliation against borrowers' filings, allows a large exposure of this kind to sit outside the view of members and regulators. It also shows how the arrangement extends the disposable church model: congregants and cooperative members carry the financial risk, while durable assets settle with a company controlled by church leaders, within a wider pattern of religious financing marked by fictitious insurance, cash couriers, and a Brazilian tax-evasion ruling.

detail.abstract: Large price moves are often preceded by intervals of abnormally low volatility and thin participation. This paper asks whether that pattern can arise endogenously from three ordinary market features: investors who stop updating beliefs when volatility is low, diffusion of beliefs through a concentrated network, and market makers who withdraw when inventory binds. We implement these features in NEXUS, an agent-based limit-order market calibrated to daily and intraday equity data, and define a silence-break event as volatility below 30 percent of baseline for at least 10 periods followed by a move exceeding two baseline standard deviations within 20 periods. The paper reports a measured computational baseline for a 2,000-period configuration and otherwise presents a mechanism with a pre-specified falsification plan: factorial ablations, synthetic parameter recovery, threshold sensitivity, placebo detectors, and time-separated validation. A pilot run illustrates why the plan is necessary rather than optional. The event detector flags 1,908 windows in 2,000 periods, which reflects overlapping windows rather than independent episodes and invalidates any exceedance rate computed before deduplication. Excess kurtosis of 501.4 further indicates pathological tails that a binary fit flag cannot summarize. These issues are documented with the corresponding remedies. The contribution is therefore a testable mechanism, an identification design, and a scale baseline-not a confirmed empirical finding.

detail.abstract: People appear to hold machines to a higher safety standard than they hold people. The usual explanation is bias. This paper shows that part of such a standard can be rational. People can help after their own failures in situations nobody anticipated, whereas machines help only where its program specifies how or where it generalises correctly from an objective. When liability is incomplete, and guarantees of help are costly, guilt about breaching a duty to help and agent-regret about harm one has caused can boost incentives. An informed customer can then rationally require a machine to fail less often than a person. The requirement is bounded by the share of the loss that help removes, focuses on failure rates rather than final harm, and scales with the machine service; at scale, it survives only where people handle unforeseeable situations more reliably than machines. For a given pattern of help, guilt is the less costly motive because it is felt only on breach. Duties can be assigned to a human responder; agency cannot.

detail.abstract: Cross-entity industrial collaboration (predictive maintenance, cross-plant quality control, supply-chain coordination) is blocked by data confidentiality; industrial time series are non-IID and multi-scale. Federated learning (FL) resolves the ownership conflict, but updates leak under gradient-inversion attacks, and deployments must cope with uneven client quality and node churn. This paper presents a privacy-preserving FL framework for industrial time series: (i) variance-adaptive multi-scale feature enhancement with a parameter-bounded gated unit (MSTGU); (ii) DMAE, a dropout-resilient privacy layer masking each gradient afresh with unilateral PRF masks, encrypting the quality-weighted masked gradient under a shared CKKS key, and threshold-decrypting exactly two aggregate sums—confining the server to the aggregate-only view (semi-honest honest-majority, t_d = ⌈2N/3⌉, collusion ≤ t_d − 1); and (iii) trust-aware aggregation with server-checkable signals, outlier screening, and rank normalization capping any client’s weight share at 2/(N+1). On four benchmarks (synthetic series, CWRU, Tennessee Eastman, and the Online Retail II stream—a single-retailer proxy; 5–20 seeds, real SEAL loop, four intensities), the per-client view lets the attacker approach true samples (error 0.7–2.1), while the aggregate-only view keeps the error at 52–970 (616.6–5,531.6 in the strongest-attack setting); masking and encryption cost no measurable accuracy (two-one-sided equivalence test, p = 0.011); 30–50% dropout retains 100.1–100.3% accuracy (99.5% on Online Retail); and the manipulation channel is significant at scale, closed by server-verified evaluation (honest-simulation; p < 0.0001).

detail.abstract: Contemporary sociological theory operates as an obsolete diagnostic exercise. Frozen in midtwentieth-century qualitative paradigms, mainstream scholarship treats human collectives through the romantic lens of voluntary social contracts, communicative rationality, and discursive negotiation, leaving the analytical apparatus entirely blind to the raw physical mechanics of systemic collapse. This paper dismantles this reductionist framework by formalizing Sociotectonics-an emergent engineering discipline that conceptualizes civilization as a dynamic thermodynamic system anchored upon non-compressible structural foundations designated as Social Plates: Resources, Identity, Security, and Hierarchy. Moving beyond the predictive impotence of traditional qualitative methods, the model translates social cohesion into measurable ratios of stress, density, and entropic decay. By shifting the analytical nexus from subjective human intent to the measurement of sub-surface tectonic strain, social viscosity, and energy dissipation, Sociotectonics establishes a rigorous quantitative architecture for calculating institutional rupture and forecasting civilizational realignment. The structural failure of late-modern governance stems directly from its refusal to evaluate the physical costs of institutional complexity. While classical sociological traditions treat legal frameworks, democratic rituals, and bureaucratic apparatuses as autonomous spheres of human agency, Sociotectonics demonstrates that surface institutions are merely passive extensions residing above deep-level energetic and physical collisions. When political elites execute top-down legislative interventions without accounting for the friction accumulating across underlying Social Plates, they generate massive structural distortion. As entropic decay accelerates and communication channels within administrative hierarchies become saturated with noise, the energetic yield of systemic complexity declines below the cost of its maintenance. By operationalizing thermodynamic laws alongside algorithmic modeling, Sociotectonics strips away the therapeutic rhetoric of humanistic sociology to engineer resilient, self-sustaining socio-technical architectures capable of absorbing severe planetary and structural shocks. Voluntary compliance is an ideological illusion; human collectives obey the unyielding laws of stress, spatial density, and thermodynamic decay.

title: A Quantitative Model for Assessing the Role of Interbank Solidarity Agreements in a Deposit Insurance System
affiliations: Universita di Cagliari, Universita di Cagliari and Università degli Studi di Cagliari

detail.title: A Quantitative Model for Assessing the Role of Interbank Solidarity Agreements in a Deposit Insurance System
detail.abstract:
Deposit Guarantee Schemes (DGSs) are a cornerstone of depositor protection and financial stability.
Assessing their adequate financial capacity, however, requires considering not only the volume of covered
deposits but also the risk profile of member institutions and the dependence of losses across the banking system.
Mutual support arrangements among banks are generally treated as a qualitative feature of the institutional
deposit protection architecture. Their economic value for depositor protection, and in particular the extent to
which they reduce the potential demand placed on a DGS, has received much less attention.
This paper proposes a framework for quantifying the DGS-equivalent value of interbank solidarity agreements.
In the model, solidarity resources intervene before the DGS by absorbing losses that would otherwise lead a
member bank in a distress state, thereby reducing both the frequency and the size of residual demands on the
DGS.
Using the SYMBOL simulation model on a panel of 199 Italian cooperative banks in 2024, we show how a
given solidarity capacity can be translated into an equivalent reduction in the DGS funding requirement under
a constant depositor-safety criterion, and conversely how much solidarity capacity is required to sustain a given
model-implied DGS funding ratio.

detail.abstract: In India, high-stakes centralized entrance examinations like NEET-UG are characterized by artificial scarcity and have been plagued by recurrent paper leaks, which exacerbate educational inequalities. Despite the passage of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act 2024, state responses have largely focused on punitive deterrence while avoiding systemic reform. This paper analyzes the aftermath of the 2026 NEET-UG paper leaks and the emergence of the "Cockroach Janta Party" (CJP), an informal, youth-led collective that mobilized mass protests against institutional failures. Utilizing Kingdon's Multiple Streams Framework and Hood and Margetts' NATO typology, the study examines how CJP, despite lacking formal authority or financial resources, leveraged digital nodality and grassroots organization to shift the issue from a societal concern to the decision-making agenda. The analysis reveals that while the movement achieved significant political accountability, culminating in the historic resignation of the Union Education Minister, the resulting policy window was primarily utilized by the state to reinforce technology-driven and punitive measures rather than addressing structural rent-seeking. Ultimately, the campaign disrupted a long-standing norm of youth apathy, demonstrating that sustained public pressure can successfully breach institutional armor.

detail.abstract: The construction industry is undergoing rapid digital transformation, making digital project management (DPM) systems increasingly vital for improving organizational performance. Anchored on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, this quantitative explanatory study examined the relationship between DPM adoption and administrative efficiency in a Philippine construction company. Data were collected from 135 project personnel, including project engineers, QA engineers, safety officers, and document controllers, using a validated structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and Pearson product-moment correlation were used for data analysis. Findings revealed high levels of DPM adoption among respondents, indicating consistent use of digital platforms for documentation, communication, and daily project administration. Administrative efficiency was also rated high across four dimensions-document management, communication, task coordination, and reporting-with document management showing the strongest performance. Correlation analysis confirmed a statistically significant positive relationship between DPM adoption and administrative efficiency, indicating that increased use of digital tools enhances workflow efficiency, communication flow, and coordination effectiveness. However, respondents also reported moderate operational challenges. Site-level friction points such as software instability and inconsistent connectivity hinder optimization, demonstrating that technological, organizational, and environmental conditions jointly influence system effectiveness under the TOE framework. Consequently, proposed managerial interventions prioritize offline-capable functionalities, structured role-specific training, and standardized workflows using automated responsibility matrices to enhance DPM adoption and administrative efficiency. Based on these results, the study recommends strengthening digital infrastructure, improving system reliability, implementing structured role-specific training, and enhancing managerial coordination through standardized digital workflows. These interventions aim to sustain and maximize the efficiency gains of digital project management adoption in construction operations.

title: Predictive Modelling and Optimization of Sugarcane Yield under Climatic Variability using Response Surface Methodology: Evidence from Chiredzi District, Zimbabwe

affiliations.org_name: The National University of Science and Technology (NUST) - National University of Science and Technology

detail.abstract: Climate variability poses a significant challenge to sustainable sugarcane production, particularly in semi-arid regions such as south-eastern Zimbabwe. This study developed a predictive and optimization model for sugarcane yield under variable climatic conditions using Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Field and secondary data from Chiredzi sugarcane estates were used, incorporating key agronomic variables (nitrogen fertilizer, irrigation levels, and planting density) alongside environmental variables (temperature and rainfall). A Central Composite Design (CCD) was employed to generate experimental runs, and a second-order polynomial model was fitted to quantify the relationships between variables and yield. Results indicated that both agronomic and climatic variables significantly influenced sugarcane yield (p < 0.05). However, interaction effects were found insignificant, while the quadratic terms proved valuable. The lack of fit of the initial model comprising linear, interaction, and quadratic terms necessitated removal of the interaction terms, resulting in a statistically significant model. The developed model demonstrated high predictive accuracy (R² = 0.92), indicating good model fit. Optimization analysis revealed that yield can be improved by up to 18–25% under optimal combinations of irrigation (1328mm/season) , fertilizer (141kg/ha) , and planting density (92276 stalks/ha) adjusted to prevailing climatic conditions ( average temperatures and rainfall of 33.1°C and 472mm/season respectively). The corresponding optimal yield was 123.3 tonnes per hectare. RSM proved useful for determining optimal conditions under varying agronomic and environmental circumstances. The findings have important implications for climate-resilient agricultural management and resource optimization in the water-constrained region.

detail.abstract:
This study explored the gap between education policy and classroom practice in Northern
Nigeria, with a focus on how this gap affects girls' access to and experience of schooling.
Despite the presence of national policies such as the Universal Basic Education Act and the
National Gender Policy in Education, many girls remain excluded from education due to
poor implementation. The purpose of the study was to evaluate this policy-practice gap
and propose recommendations to strengthen implementation.

A convergent mixed-methods approach was used. Quantitative data were collected
through questionnaires administered to 50 teachers in Kaduna State using purposive
sampling. Qualitative data came from expert interviews with representatives from the
Ministries of Education and Women’s Affairs, respectively. Findings revealed low awareness
of gender-focused policies, lack of funding, weak intergovernmental coordination, and
insufficient teacher training as major barriers.

The study concluded that bridging the policy-practice gap requires localized
gender-responsive implementation plans and an independent audit body to monitor education
policy delivery. Future research should explore scalable models for cross-ministerial
collaboration and sustainable funding mechanisms for girls’ education policy
enforcement.

detail.abstract:
Only 14% of employees strongly agree that their performance reviews inspire them to improve (Gallup). One reason is that most performance management systems (PMS) judge people on parameters chosen by habit, not evidence. This practitioner's guide shows, step by step, how to build a PMS from your own data while keeping the manager's judgement in charge.

The method runs in eight steps across five parts. It checks whether the data is large enough, uses the signal-to-noise ratio to choose a selection method (following Hastie et al., 2020), and applies best subset regression to find the few parameters that actually drive the goal. These are split into Will (Effort) and Skill (Efficiency), weighted from standardised coefficients, graded against peers and combined into one composite score. Each employee is then placed on a skill/will matrix (Champion, Warrior, Specialist, Struggler), given a clear manager action, and ranked on a single dashboard.

Every step is worked through on a simulated sample of 200 FMCG promoters with 20 candidate parameters. Cutting the list to five raised cross-validated R² from .281 to .361, and the final score correlated 0.57 with net sales in the sample. A free Excel workbook with live formulas (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23158997) and ready-to-run Python code are included. Written for students, HR professionals and sales leaders who want a PMS that is fair, explainable and tied to results.

detail.abstract: The existence of technical alternatives does not establish how much additional service they can provide during a material supply disruption. This article proposes a protocol to distinguish known routes from jointly feasible additional capacity for a specified function, system, disturbance and horizon. Building on functional substitution, criticality, resilience and viability research, the procedure requires verifiable requirements, uncommitted capacity, shared constraints and an explicit information cutoff. Its output is a conditional estimate, a justified bound or a documented decision not to estimate. A synthetic lighting replacement illustration makes inputs and calculations reproducible: including shared conversion capacity reduces feasible replacement coverage from 100% in the relaxed formulation to 86%. Cumulative service loss is 0.78%, whereas unmet replacement reaches 14%; satisfying one criterion does not imply satisfying both. This difference follows from ordinary feasibility constraints and does not demonstrate superiority over competent models. Earlier lighting, electricity and public procurement exercises are retained as development evidence and measurement limitations. The proposed contribution is to make inferences and stopping decisions auditable; usefulness with independent users and real data remains to be assessed. Technology may reduce some dependencies and create others.

detail.abstract: The offshore oil and gas environment in Africa is complex and highly risky, with issues such as equipment failure potentially halting production, impacting maintenance costs, and posing safety and environmental risks. The study compares among four maintenance approaches which are corrective/reactive maintenance, preventive maintenance, reliability centered maintenance (RCM) and predictive or condition-based maintenance (CBM) paying special attention on their applicability to African offshore operations. The study brings together the findings of these previous maintenance studies, as well as documented case studies from offshore environments in Nigeria and Angola (and other West African settings). Offshore maintenance optimization is a multiple objective problem regarding the equipment reliability, maintenance cost, personnel availability, logistics, environment and safety (George, Loo and Jie). An African study of the benefits of preventive and predictive maintenance showed that this strategy could cut unplanned downtime by about 40-50% from reactive maintenance, and a model-based hybrid maintenance approach offered around 98% equipment availability (Uke). The combined application of combined curative and condition-based maintenance over systematic preventive maintenance (SPIE) is illustrated in Angola. The results indicate that a single maintenance philosophy is not the optimum solution for effective maintenance practices in African offshore and applying high tech digital machines is not a one fits all solution. Rather, a context specific 'hybrid' method that incorporates asset criticality assessment, preventive maintenance, condition monitoring, reliability analysis, optimized scheduling, skilled personnel and appropriate digital technologies is a more flexible solution to enhance the performance of offshore assets. The research outcomes suggest that in the future maintenance should be shifted to the integration of technology capability with the local operating conditions, with workforce capacity and with the specific risk of the assets.

title: Watching the Aurora in Freezing Cold: How Unwanted Adversity Becomes an Observational Vantage Point

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the Aurora Observation Structure (AOS) to explain how an unwanted adverse environment can acquire a second meaning as an observational vantage point while remaining a source of burden. Previous research on posttraumatic growth, meaning making, and sensemaking has examined how individuals psychologically respond to difficult experiences. Less attention, however, has been paid to how an involuntary change in social or organizational position can alter what becomes observable.

AOS begins with Imposed Cold, a condition in which a person is moved into an unwanted or disadvantageous position. This shift may lead to an Observer Position Shift, followed by Relational Access Reconfiguration, Institutional Layer Exposure, and Structural Visibility Expansion. As relationships, information pathways, decision processes, and institutional mechanisms become newly visible, the individual may begin to observe patterns that were previously embedded in the background of ordinary participation. When these observations are supported by an Observation Infrastructure consisting of longitudinal records, comparison, engagement with existing research, reflexivity, and external critique, episodic experiences may become more systematic and examinable forms of knowledge.

The central claim of AOS is not that adversity produces growth, creativity, or knowledge. Adversity may instead produce exhaustion, withdrawal, silence, or harm. Even when observational value emerges, the original burden does not disappear. AOS therefore conceptualizes the outcome not as Adversity → Benefit, but as the coexistence of Adversity and Observational Value. This non-cancellation principle separates the ethical evaluation of harmful conditions from the epistemic value that may later emerge from observing them.

AOS is thus presented not as a theory that celebrates suffering, but as a limited conceptual model of how involuntary positional change can modify structural visibility and, under certain conditions, create an opportunity for knowledge generation. The metaphor of watching an aurora in freezing cold captures this duality: seeing something valuable does not make the cold desirable, nor does the cold become justified because something became visible within it.

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is reducing the execution cost of many activities in advertising, design, content production, and other knowledge-intensive business services. Most managerial responses focus on intra-firm automation: performing the same work faster, with fewer resources. This paper distinguishes intra-firm automation from inter-firm production architecture and examines a different adaptive response: buyer-side pooling of modular professional services. The focal arrangement occurs when independent buyers jointly commission and fund a reusable service layer while retaining separate control over firm-specific modules such as brand, offer, pricing, customer data, and local adaptation. The paper situates this arrangement at the intersection of transaction cost economics, cooperative purchasing and co-commissioning, and service modularity. It derives a viability condition in which the real resource savings from avoiding duplicated common-layer work must exceed the cost of producing a coalition-wide shared layer plus coordination, heterogeneity, delay, differentiation, and residual risk costs. AI's net effect is therefore conditional rather than uniformly positive: pooling becomes more viable only when AI-induced reductions in coalition-side costs, including the cost of the shared layer, outweigh the pooling benefit lost as independent production itself becomes cheaper. Aggregate surplus is also insufficient for stability; required buyers and suppliers must each prefer participation to their outside option. The paper distinguishes resource efficiency from monetary transfers among buyers, suppliers, and coordinating intermediaries, and identifies governance, competition-law, and intellectual-property boundary conditions. It does not claim empirical validation; its contribution is a falsifiable conceptual framework and research agenda for subsequent field testing.

title: AI Won't Replace Universities -But It May Unbundle Them

detail.abstract: Debate about generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has focused primarily on teaching, assessment, academic integrity, and the changing role of educators. This paper argues that this framing captures only part of AI's institutional significance. Universities are not simply providers of instruction. They bundle teaching, tutoring, assessment, credentialing, research, administration, professional formation, networks, and institutional reputation within a single organizational form. The relevant question is therefore not only how AI changes education, but whether it changes the economic rationale for keeping these functions bundled together. The paper develops the concept of scarcity reversal to explain this possibility. Generative AI can make some forms of intellectual assistance, explanation, drafting, and information processing substantially more abundant and scalable while simultaneously increasing the relative value of functions that remain difficult to automate or whose value depends on human or institutional trust. As explanation becomes abundant, judgement may become relatively scarce; as routine tutoring becomes scalable, mentorship may become more valuable; and as sophisticated outputs become easier to generate, credible verification of individual competence may become more important. Building on earlier scholarship on the unbundling of higher education and emerging evidence on AI-assisted knowledge work, the paper argues that AI should be understood not as a uniform substitute for university labour but as a technology that changes the relative costs and scarcity of different components of the university bundle. This produces three possible institutional trajectories: the augmented university, in which AI increases productivity while existing institutional boundaries remain largely intact; the transformed university, in which AI changes the internal division of labour and relative importance of university functions; and the unbundled university, in which functions increasingly migrate to specialized providers outside the institution. The argument is not that technological change makes the university obsolete. It is that AI may change the relative economics of university functions sufficiently to reopen a more fundamental question: which functions still need to be bundled together within the institution we call a university, and why?

detail.abstract: This paper argues that the expansion of human activity into outer space should be guided by intentional ethical practices rather than ad hoc developments built around crises, profit margins, or political strength. detail.abstract: This paper shows that trade wars weaken managerial incentives, a key driver of firm productivity. It embeds a principal-agent problem in a two-country trade model with heterogeneous firms. Owners pay managers to reduce costs, and the optimal contract varies with the firm's initial productivity. Matched CEO-firm data for U.S. manufacturers support the model's predictions: incentive pay is hump-shaped in firm productivity, and its heterogeneous response to trade policy comes mainly from the tariffs U.S. exporters face abroad rather than from U.S. import tariffs. In the estimated model, a trade war strengthens incentives for less productive firms that sell only at home and weakens them for exporters, most strongly near the export margin. In the aggregate, incentives fall, and productivity and output decline by 6.5% and 5%, respectively. Models that omit managerial incentives miss about four fifths of the output cost of a trade war.

detail.abstract: The integration of advanced analytics capabilities within enterprise human capital management platforms has emerged as a transformative force in contemporary human resource management, yet the extent to which platforms such as SAP SuccessFactors enable meaningful HR analytics adoption and organizational value creation remains inadequately synthesized. This study conducts a systematic review of the literature examining SAP SuccessFactors and its role in shaping the future of HR analytics, addressing a critical gap in understanding how cloud-based HCM platforms facilitate data-driven decision-making across the employee lifecycle. While prior research has examined HR analytics adoption and AI-driven HRIS transformation in isolation, the specific contribution of SAP SuccessFactors as an integrated analytics-enabling platform has not been comprehensively reviewed. This systematic review follows PRISMA guidelines, synthesizing peer-reviewed studies, conference proceedings, and industry research published between 2015 and 2024 that address SAP SuccessFactors implementation, HR analytics capabilities, and organizational outcomes. The analysis identifies key thematic clusters including platform-enabled analytics maturity, integration of AI and machine learning capabilities, workforce planning and predictive modeling, and persistent challenges related to data quality, skills gaps, and ethical governance. Findings indicate that SAP SuccessFactors provides a foundation for HR analytics through its integrated module architecture and embedded reporting capabilities, but that organizations vary substantially in their realization of analytical value, with many remaining at descriptive rather than predictive or prescriptive analytics stages. The review also reveals significant gaps in empirical evidence regarding the causal relationship between SAP SuccessFactors adoption and organizational performance outcomes, and identifies emerging research directions including agentic AI integration, ethical algorithm governance, and cross-cultural analytics implementation. The findings contribute to theoretical understanding of technology-enabled HR transformation and offer practical guidance for organizations seeking to advance their HR analytics capabilities through SAP SuccessFactors adoption and optimization.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming service systems to improve efficiency. However, its adoption often coincides with rising customer complaints about service failures and long waits. Using call centers as a representative case, this study investigates how AI affects operational costs and customer welfare. We develop an analytical framework in which the service system is modeled as a large-scale multi-server queueing system, where customers are heterogeneous in request complexity. The service provider jointly optimizes staffing levels and the allocation of customer requests between AI and human servers. Our analysis shows that although AI adoption reduces total costs and staffing requirements, it inevitably lengthens the expected waiting time in the human server queue due to the loss of economies of scale. Consequently, customers with high request complexity may find themselves worse off. Furthermore, we find a counterintuitive relationship where a decrease in AI-related costs will further deteriorate the experience for these customers by inducing the firm to shift more load toward AI. We then identify a conflict between the service provider and customers regarding the preferred scope of AI adoption. Imposing a waiting-time constraint on the human-server queue effectively mitigates this conflict, and the resulting gain in customer welfare substantially exceeds the associated increase in the total cost.

detail.abstract:
Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 — the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) — created the EU's first
comprehensive crypto-asset framework. Title III governs asset-referenced tokens (ARTs). The category
emerged largely from concern about large stablecoins, but was drafted broadly enough to cover tokens
linked to many values or rights, including physical assets. More than two years after the ART rules became
applicable, the ESMA register contains zero authorised ARTs. This paper argues that physical, non-financial
reserves expose a mismatch between that broad definition and parts of the compliance framework. Article
36 permits mark-to-model valuation where reliable market prices are unavailable, but does not provide a
methodology tailored to heterogeneous physical assets. Article 39 requires cash or in-kind redemption
while prohibiting redemption fees. For illiquid physical reserves, those rules create unresolved valuation,
liquidity and delivery problems. The Article 16(2)(a) small-issuer exemption provides a workable route but
limits average outstanding token value to €5 million. Using GNRC, backed by Greenlandic rubies and
sapphires, this paper identifies three structural problems and proposes targeted reforms for the current
MiCA review.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the paradox of securities-fraud class actions as both an important private-enforcement mechanism and a source of agency costs, settlement abuse, circular wealth transfers, and market punishment. It analyzes the theoretical foundations of class litigation, including the conflict between aggregate representation and individual litigant autonomy, the lawyer-driven character of class actions, attorneys' fee incentives, judicial scrutiny of fee awards, and the role of directors' and officers' liability insurance in settlement. It then discusses settlement dynamics under Rule 23 and the PSLRA, emphasizing courts' role in policing collusion, red-flag settlement terms, excessive fees, broad releases, and premature resolutions. It further evaluates the broader effects of securities-fraud class actions on corporations, shareholders, management, and stakeholders, including reputational harm, stock-price declines, derivative suits, ERISA claims, insider-trading litigation, and SEC enforcement. Finally, the paper reviews proposed reforms, including claim-alienability models, online dispute resolution, opt-in settlement structures, regulatory sanctions, officer-liability reforms, mandatory arbitration, whistleblower enforcement, derivative-treatment proposals, shareholder voting mechanisms, and reconsideration of the fraud-on-the-market presumption. It concludes that any serious reform must confront the recurring problems of litigation scale, agency costs, and circular wealth transfers, while also accounting for artificial intelligence and the changing information environment that increasingly challenges traditional assumptions of information asymmetry.

detail.abstract:
Printed wallcoverings combine decoration with surface function, but the expectations placed on them are expanding. Beyond visual appeal, many interior applications now demand resistance to moisture, abrasion, contamination, surface deterioration, and microbial colonization. Conventional coatings can provide several of these functions, yet many depend on petroleum-derived polymers, synthetic additives, and solvent-intensive processing. This has increased interest in renewable alternatives, including bio-based polymers, lignin, cellulose-derived materials, plant-oil components, proteins, bio-based polyesters, and water-based coating systems [1–5].
Against this background, this article explores the development of a bio-based antimicrobial coating specifically for printed wallcoverings. The central concern is not antimicrobial activity alone, but how that function interacts with print quality, surface behavior, coating durability, formulation stability, and sustainability. The proposed system is treated as a multifunctional coating. The framework covers material selection, antimicrobial incorporation, formulation and application, antimicrobial testing, print-quality assessment, surface characterization, adhesion, durability, and statistical analysis.
Previous studies show that bio-based coatings can provide useful barrier, mechanical, surface-functional, and antimicrobial properties, but their performance depends strongly on material chemistry, antimicrobial concentration, dispersion, substrate characteristics, coating thickness, drying conditions, and processing [1–7]. Work on lignin- and cellulose-based systems also points to gains in water resistance, oil resistance, mechanical reinforcement, barrier behavior, and surface functionality [2,3]. At the same time, bio-based polymer blends can introduce their own difficulties, including compatibility problems, phase separation, limited flexibility, processability issues, and changes in mechanical stability [4,5].
The central challenge, then, is to balance biological effectiveness with the practical requirements of the wallcovering. A coating may strongly inhibit microorganisms and still perform poorly if it causes excessive color change, loss of gloss, weak adhesion, cracking, brittleness, or poor abrasion resistance. The reverse is also true: a visually attractive and mechanically sound coating is of little value if its antimicrobial activity is inadequate. For that reason, antimicrobial function, print preservation, surface protection, durability, and sustainability are treated here as connected performance requirements. 
No original experimental measurements were supplied for the proposed printed-wallcovering system, so numerical results are not invented in this article. Instead, the Results and Evaluation framework identifies the measurements and indicators that should be reported once the experimental work is completed. The framework is intended to establish an evidence-based way to determine whether a bio-based antimicrobial coating can provide microbial-control functionality while preserving appearance, adhesion, mechanical integrity, surface performance, and practical usability [1,6–8]. More broadly, the study seeks to support the development of sustainable functional interior surfaces in which renewable materials and antimicrobial technology can work together without sacrificing the essential characteristics of printed wallcoverings.

detail.abstract: Affecting an estimated 0.85% of India’s population, approximately 12.5 million citizens, speech dysfluency remains subject to systemic socio-economic exclusion driven by restrictive legislative frameworks and public health deficits. Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, statutory protections mandate a rigid 40% medical impairment threshold, effectively disenfranchising Persons Who Stammer (PWS) with covert or situational dysfluency. This structural exclusion is compounded by the omission of PWS from Section 34 public employment quotas and the enforcement of blanket medical disqualifications across high-stakes public services, including the Armed Forces and the Indian Police Service (IPS). This policy brief evaluates potential reforms across statutory, functional, and administrative dimensions. While expanding statutory public employment quotas offers direct economic empowerment, it risks provoking intense resource-distribution conflicts with existing protected disability groups over the highly contested 4% reservation pool. Conversely, adopting a United Kingdom-style functional assessment model presents an equitable, long-term ideological goal, but immediate implementation is constrained by a severe national shortage of Speech-Language Pathologists (SLPs). To circumvent legislative gridlock and deliver actionable relief, this brief recommends a dual-track, fiscally neutral administrative framework. First, the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) should mandate non-zero-sum procedural accommodations, specifically granting compensatory extra time to PWS during high-stakes oral evaluations and public service interviews. Mirroring existing provisions for visually impaired candidates, this establishes a merit-based, accessible evaluation standard. Second, the Ministry of Education should integrate speech dysfluency metrics into the UDISE+ database. By utilizing primary schools as frontline screening nodes—the state can efficiently generate its first longitudinal dataset on paediatric stuttering. Ultimately, this hybrid strategy ensures immediate career mobility for adult PWS while constructing the foundational data architecture necessary to facilitate future systemic reforms.

detail.abstract:
Financial decision-support tasks place unusual demands on language models: they combine domain-specific language, numerical reasoning, policy interpretation, tool use, and structured cross-asset analysis. FinVector-Market-4B is a compact financial-reasoning adaptation of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B trained with rank-16 LoRA on a frozen 22,000-example corpus. The corpus combines externally grounded central-bank and FinQA records with project-generated FinMath and structural market-reasoning supervision, all normalized into a common system/user/assistant format with leakage-safe group splitting. The base model remains frozen during training; 21.23 million LoRA parameters are updated across attention and feed-forward projections over one BF16 training epoch.

A central evaluation challenge is separating genuine task adaptation from learning the response contract. We therefore evaluate both the base and fine-tuned model under two matched prompt conditions: an implicit FinVector contract and an explicit task-specific JSON schema. Supplying the schema alone raises basemodel JSON validity from 0% to 91.3%, showing that prompt compliance explains a substantial share of the zero-shot failure mode. Yet large gains remain under the matched explicit-schema control: FinQA exact match improves from 14.7% to 40.0%, correct calculator-expression accuracy from 48.0% to 82.7%, calculator answer tolerance from 8.0% to 44.0%, scenario-direction agreement from 20.1% to 89.5%, and structural implication-direction agreement from 52.4% to 87.2%. Not every metric improves: policy-tone macro-F1 falls from 77.4% to 62.3% despite a rise in overall accuracy from 80.0% to 84.0%. The results show that compact financial domain adaptation can produce substantial task-specific gains beyond outputformat learning, while prompt design and metric choice remain consequential for evaluating financial AI systems.

title: Back to First Principles: Towards a Theory of Process Improvement for the Digital Age

detail.abstract: Process improvement is central to operations management, yet our understanding of improvement remains tied to the methods through which it has historically been practised. Research has focused on the effectiveness of improvement methods and the practices that improve performance; it emphasizes differences among methods rather than identifying the common logic underlying improvement. Historically, this gap was obscured because improvement methods emerged as integrated systems of philosophies, principles, practices, and socio-technical arrangements. Digital technologies expose it: they arrive as general-purpose capabilities, providing instruments for change without specifying what constitutes improvement, how it should be pursued, or what is required to sustain it. We address this gap by returning to first principles. We formalize the conceptual foundations of process improvement and identify four principles as "common denominators" that characterize improvement across methods and contexts. We then apply these principles to digital technologies to clarify what they contribute to improvement, what they lack, and what firms must provide to translate technological capability into sustained operational improvement. Our aim is to provide a generic theoretical foundation for understanding process improvement independent of any particular method and, in doing so, a basis for making sense of the emerging role of digital technologies in improving operations.

detail.abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) separates the control plane from the data plane and exposes a logically centralized, programmable view of network state. This architecture creates a natural setting for data-driven control, yet most production controllers still rely on static policies, heuristics, or analytically tractable optimization models that struggle with volatile traffic and heterogeneous service requirements. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an alternative: an agent learns resource-allocation policies through interaction with the network, guided by a reward signal rather than labelled examples. This paper reviews the peer-reviewed literature on RL-based resource orchestration in SDN, covering routing and traffic engineering, network slicing, and cross-domain resource management. We organize existing work by learning paradigm, orchestration task, and deployment assumptions, and we compare value-based, policy-gradient, actor-critic, multi-agent, and model-augmented approaches. The review identifies recurring gaps: dependence on simulation, weak treatment of safety during exploration, limited generalization across topologies, scalability of centralized agents, and the absence of standardized benchmarks. We then propose a conceptual, layered framework that combines graphbased state representation, constrained policy learning, and hierarchical multi-agent coordination, together with a staged validation pathway. The framework is presented as a research agenda, not as an implemented or validated system. The paper closes with practical implications for operators and directions for future work. No new experiments are reported; all empirical claims are attributed to the cited sources.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates how the ownership structures of Chinese enterprises shape their outward foreign direct investment (OFDI) outcomes, and whether corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance alters that relationship. Drawing on agency theory and a firm-level panel dataset of companies listed on China's Shenzhen and Shanghai Stock Exchanges covering 2008 to 2017, the study asks two related questions: does state ownership systematically disadvantage firms in international investment relative to their privately held counterparts, and does CSR performance function as a moderating force capable of offsetting whatever ownership-driven effects emerge? The empirical analysis indicates that state-owned enterprises (SOEs) tend to underperform private firms in OFDI, yet reveals that the degree of government intervention, whether a firm is controlled by the central government or by a provincial or municipal authority, does not itself produce a statistically distinguishable difference in OFDI outcomes within the SOE category. Crucially, the study finds that stronger CSR performance can partially offset the OFDI disadvantage associated with state ownership, but this moderating effect is not uniform across all SOEs: it operates specifically among locally governed SOEs, whose primary obstacle in foreign markets is a reputational deficit rather than the institutional pressure and risk aversion that constrain centrally governed counterparts.

detail.abstract: How costly is uniform congestion pricing when locations differ in value? I study geostationary orbit, where satellites serve different markets from recorded positions and supported $77 billion in satellite television revenues in 2023. I estimate a spatial model of commercial entry in which efficient charges rise with demand. In the baseline estimates, the optimal uniform charge captures 66 percent of the attainable welfare gain, or 79 percent when income replaces population as the demand measure. It reduces congestion but ends entry at positions accounting for less than a tenth of modeled efficient surplus. Longitude-specific charges recover the rest while preserving entry at marginal positions. Most additional gains arise at positions the uniform charge keeps active. Correcting underpricing at high-demand positions contributes the largest share. Substantial spatial heterogeneity can therefore coexist with large gains from a common price, whose cost depends on the surplus exposed to its pricing errors.

detail.abstract:
Problem definition: The inventory ordering process of small retailers in developing countries is rapidly undergoing a digital transformation. Facilitated by large-scale smartphone access, suppliers have complemented the traditional presales agent with additional ordering channels, such as call centers and mobile apps. These channels may boost sales by increasing the number of ordering options, but they may also disrupt established sales and distribution processes.

Methodology/results: In collaboration with a Moroccan CPG distributor, we use a staggered difference-in-differences design with not-yet-treated controls to estimate the effects of call center activation for nanostores that previously ordered through the presales agent and of mobile app adoption for nanostores that previously ordered through the call center. Call center activation, which is predominantly supplier-initiated, increases order frequency and total order value at the focal distributor, although roughly 40\% of the additional call center orders displace presales agent orders. Mobile app adoption increases order frequency and total order value without displacing orders in existing channels and broadens the assortment ordered. Neither channel raises the store-level rejection rate, and the gains accrue predominantly to smaller and less active nanostores. Because more than 95\% of call center contacts are outbound and app uptake remains limited, ordering remains largely supplier-triggered. A stylized model shows that the average distance between stores is essential in determining whether a supplier should trigger orders through a presales or a call center agent.

Managerial implications: Our results help managers understand the impact of introducing new ordering channels and design the multichannel ordering process of nanostores. Unlike in business-to-consumer settings, where additional channels typically reduce customer effort, new channels in this business-to-business setting differ in whether they leave the ordering initiative with the supplier or require shopkeepers to order on their own initiative. This distinction shapes their value: a channel that relies on supplier-initiated contact, like the presales agent, partly reallocates existing orders, whereas a channel through which nanostores order on their own initiative captures additional demand. Since ordering remains largely supplier-triggered, suppliers should continue to trigger orders actively, target new channels at smaller and less active nanostores, and account for store density when allocating capacity between presales and call center agents. These insights are particularly relevant given the significant efforts made to digitalize the ordering process of nanostores in practice.

detail.abstract: Decision-makers in learning environments face a dilemma when their short-term optimal actions may not favor their long-term benefits the most. To understand the fundamental tradeoff behind the dilemma, we study adaptive experimentation with post-commitment reward shifts. During an experiment phase, the decision-maker may adaptively test multiple options; during a subsequent commitment phase, the decision-maker must commit to a single option, whose reward may differ from its pre-commitment reward. We propose the Reserved Arm Eliminations for Commitment (RAEC) algorithm, which reserves a predetermined portion of the experiment phase to identify the best post-shift option while using the remaining rounds to minimize short-run regret. We establish regret upper bounds for RAEC across all parameter regimes and matching minimax lower bounds, providing a tight characterization of the cost of balancing short-term performance and long-term commitment. A key implication is that deciding in advance how much of the experiment phase to reserve for the commitment decision is sufficient to achieve the best possible worst-case regret rate; adapting this amount as more data are observed does not improve the rate. We further study extensions with structural knowledge of reward shifts and with concave commitment rewards and portfolio choice. Numerical experiments confirm that our proposed algorithms achieve the regret predicted by our theory and outperform other baselines.

detail.abstract: The historical development, current framework, and future trajectory of pangolin protection in Chinese law remains notably underexplored. Drawing on legislative texts, judicial decisions, and empirical case analysis, the study identifies three key stages in China's pangolin protection regime: from solely utilization evolving into judicial protection. The historical retrospective analysis emphasizes how legislative inconsistencies historically hindered effective protection, particularly due to the medicinal use of pangolins in traditional Chinese medicine. Notably, the rise of environmental public interest litigation and the increased valuation of pangolins' ecological function significantly reshaped judicial practice. We argue that judicial mechanisms-especially civil public interest lawsuits-are becoming the primary pathway for pangolin protection in China. While substantial progress has been made, challenges remain in standardizing valuations, curating a public interest litigation regime, and developing differentiated approaches to minor and organized crimes. The article contributes practically, suggesting targeted reforms to enhance pangolin protection within China's broader ecological governance framework.

title: Gambling for Retirement: The Hidden Costs of Savings Lotteries in a Nationwide Experiment

detail.abstract: Governments increasingly encourage socially desirable behavior with probabilistic incentives. We study such "Pigouvian lotteries'' in a retirement-savings field experiment with 387,000 workers in Colombia's public pension system. The lotteries induce sharp bunching at qualification thresholds, but workers mostly meet them by retiming rather than increasing deposits, leaving overall savings largely unaffected. Lotteries further crowd out valuable life and disability insurance and disproportionately reward wealthier savers. A welfare analysis shows that, once we account for these unintended consequences, lotteries reduce welfare. Our findings illustrate that behavioral spillovers across time and choice domains can reverse the verdict on behavioral public policies.

detail.abstract: Production accounts record sectoral expenditures, but gains from reallocating labor and capital depend on technology the accounts do not reveal. In a Cobb-Douglas production network, the accounts alone cannot rule out that the observed allocation is efficient. We derive a sharp lower bound: the smallest gain from optimal reallocation across technologies consistent with the accounts and maintained restrictions. For China in 2010-2016, with relative input elasticities allowed to range from one-twelfth to twelve times their firm-based reference values, the baseline lower bound is 0.43 to 0.75 percent of real final use. The allocations behind these bounds move labor mainly from agriculture and public services into manufacturing. The positive bound depends on reference values in a few manufacturing sectors, returns-to-scale ceilings in labor-intensive sectors, and producer prices covering marginal cost. Widening the allowed range to about 20 to 23 times admits an efficient allocation and reduces the bound to zero.

detail.abstract: Integrating renewable energy with hydrogen production enhances energy self-sufficiency and reduces reliance on traditional electricity grids. However, the variability of renewable generation-particularly solar in distributed settings-often leads to surplus electricity that is curtailed, limiting renewable-to-hydrogen effectiveness. Addressing this challenge requires predictive tools like digital twins (DTs) to anticipate surplus availability, simulate production, and support control-oriented decision-making. This paper introduces a Closed-Loop Digital Twin (CLDT) framework that integrates solar forecasting, physics-informed electrolyzer modelling, and adaptive thermal management to convert surplus solar energy into hydrogen. The CLDT combines an XGBoostbased solar irradiance forecasting model, an electrochemical model to estimate hydrogen output, and a thermal model for stack temperature prediction. A residential-scale case study illustrates how forecasted surplus energy, after accounting for household demand, can be directed to hydrogen production. The lumped thermal model was evaluated against laboratory-scale stack-surface temperature measurements using a calibration-supported comparison, achieving an RMSE of 0.82 • C and an MAE of 0.67 • C. The adaptive Proportional-Integral (PI) controller was then applied in the system-level CLDT simulation to regulate cooling under hourly PV-surplus-driven operation. Using January 2024 solar and household-demand data, the simulation showed that the stack temperature remained below the defined 40 • C shutdown threshold. Although demonstrated at residential scale through an offline software-based prototype rather than a live IoT-connected implementation, the framework provides a basis for evaluating forecastinformed hydrogen production and thermal-control behaviour under hourly variable renewable energy conditions.

title: Politicized Scientists: Credibility Cost of Political Expression on Twitter

detail.abstract: We study the reputational cost of scientists’ political expression on social media. Twitter data on 98,000 U.S. academics (2016–2022) reveal substantial engagement with politically salient issues, although most posts take no political stance. Experiments with 6,000 U.S. respondents and 135 journalists show that scientists who express political views are rated less credible than politically silent ones, with penalties increasing in the strength of expression and concentrated among ideologically opposed audiences. Both politically salient research content and explicit identity cues trigger these penalties. Surveyed scientists anticipate the penalty — indeed overestimate it — and endorse limiting political expression to their domain of expertise.

title: Blockchain Fee Policies: Quantity- vs Price-Control Design Across Protocols

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper develops an economic theory to explain the optimal choice of blockchain transaction fee policies, contrasting quantity controls (as in Bitcoin) and price controls (as in Ethereum). I model the blockchain as a decentralized platform where validators, possessing temporary monopoly power and facing uncertain operational costs, choose transactions under varying user demand. Price controls outperform quantity controls when demand volatility is significant, the correlation between marginal costs and demand is low, and validators hold substantial bargaining power — conditions aligning closely with Ethereum’s current structure following its proof-of-stake transition. Conversely, quantity controls are optimal when marginal costs positively correlate with demand and validators’ bargaining power is limited, conditions characteristic of Bitcoin’s proof-of-work model. To a first-order approximation, I characterize the dynamics of Ethereum’s fee policies: deviations from the block-size target decay with persistence such that adjustment faster than the inverse elasticity buys not faster convergence but oscillations and excess fee volatility. Using recent transaction data, I illustrate that Ethereum’s base fee adjusts more rapidly than optimal. Additionally, I derive bounds for block size targets to mitigate maximal extractable value (MEV) exploitation. These insights offer guidance for improving blockchain governance and optimizing fee policy design.

detail.abstract: Low property taxes amplify lock-in among elderly homeowners, limiting housing access for young families. Raising them reallocates housing toward the young through two channels: capitalization into lower prices reduces required downpayments for financially constrained buyers, a form of embedded leverage, while higher tax obligations raise holding costs for older owners. In our overlapping generations model, raising California’s property taxes to Texas levels increases young homeownership while decreasing elderly homeownership. Removing step-up basis also lowers elderly homeownership, suggesting their tenure is sustained by bequest tax advantages. The tax treatment of housing shapes housing allocation across generations.

detail.abstract: While the US-China trade war caused Chinese exports to the United States to drop, the contraction was far from uniform across products. Analyzing HS8-level export data within a causal forest framework, we demonstrate that China's prewar revealed comparative advantage (RCA) in the US market is the dominant driver of treatment-effect heterogeneity. Variable importance and best linear projection analyses confirm RCA's central role. Partial dependence plots reveal a non-linear threshold: export drops are moderate at low RCA levels but steepen significantly once RCA hits 3.5 or higher. Complementary difference-indifferences panel regressions confirm this pattern, showing that high-RCA products suffered disproportionate contractions. Together, our findings reveal that tariff shocks impose the greatest displacement pressure on goods where the exporting country initially enjoyed the strongest market position.

title: Trade Policy and Structural Change

detail.title: Trade Policy and Structural Change

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study how tariffs affect industrial structure and welfare in an economy where sectors are complements and preferences are nonhomothetic---two drivers of structural change. Tariffs reshape sectoral composition through relative prices, income effects, and sectoral net exports. We characterize these mechanisms analytically and quantify them in a dynamic multi-country model with capital accumulation and input-output linkages. A counterfactual 20-percentage-point increase in U.S. manufacturing tariffs raises the manufacturing value-added share by about one percentage point and increases U.S. welfare by 0.43 percent, while lowering welfare abroad; retaliation would make all countries worse off. The optimal unilateral U.S. manufacturing tariff is 20.9 percent. Comparing different preference specifications, we show that homothetic preferences without income effects overstate the U.S. welfare gains from unilateral tariff increases.

detail.abstract: The 2021-2023 European energy crisis caused by the war in Ukraine prompted broad policy interventions across energy markets. In contrast to the retail-side subsidies and public transfers implemented elsewhere, Spain and Portugal targeted the wholesale electricity market through the so-called Iberian solution. Combining wholesale market simulations with machine learning techniques, we quantify the distributional implications of the crisis and this intervention on Spanish electricity firms and consumers. The crisis shifted substantial wealth from consumers to generators: power plant profits rose by € 29 Billion. Even accounting for the Iberian solution and the accompanying energy-saving measures, the crisis remained highly regressive — the lowest income quintile lost 3.4% of disposable income, three times the relative burden of the highest quintile. Without interventions, the crisis would have been considerably more costly for all households. Further, the policy package delivered proportionally larger relief to lower-income groups, at no net fiscal cost.

detail.abstract: Background and Objective: Accurate multi-class segmentation of pediatric cardiovascular anatomy is challenging because of congenital anatomical variability, small-caliber vessels, and heterogeneous imaging protocols. This exploratory study compared 3D U-Net, V-Net, Swin-UNet, and nnU-Net using a public pediatric cardiac MRI benchmark (HVSMR-2.0; n = 60) and a clinically curated multi-center cohort (n = 50; 48 CT and 2 MRI), also evaluated jointly (n = 110).,Methods: HVSMR-2.0 used 50/5/5 training/validation/test subjects, while the combined-cohort experiment used 92/10/8 subjects. Images were resampled to 1.0-mm isotropic spacing and segmented into aorta, cardiac chambers, and pulmonary arteries. Performance was assessed using overlap, boundary, and surface measures, with exploratory paired subject-level statistical comparisons.,Results: In the final combined-cohort comparison, mean foreground DSC values were 0.8200 for 3D U-Net, 0.8317 for V-Net, 0.8298 for Swin-UNet, and 0.8348 for nnU-Net. Pulmonary arteries were the most challenging class. Given the small held-out test sets, numerical differences were interpreted descriptively and did not establish model superiority or equivalence.,Conclusions: The findings provide an exploratory comparison of configured 3D segmentation systems under heterogeneous pediatric imaging conditions. Larger independent, source-stratified validation is needed before claims of generalization or deployment readiness.

detail.abstract: Informal and vulnerable employment is the bulk of work across Sub-Saharan Africa, yet whether it is a temporary stepping-stone or a self-reinforcing trap is unresolved, because high persistence in aggregate data may reflect dependence on prior status or persistent differences between workers. Distinguishing the two requires individual panel data the region has largely lacked. Using Ghana's Annual Household Income and Expenditure Survey, which re-interviews households across four quarters each year from 2022 to 2024, I estimate dynamic random-effects probit models with a Wooldridge correction for initial conditions. Most observed persistence in vulnerable employment is spurious, but positive conditional state dependence survives, strongest in urban areas and among secondary-educated workers, and is model-dependent rather than a quasi-experimental causal effect. State dependence peaks not in the 2022 crisis year but in the 2023 adjustment year that followed. This raises a policy question about maintaining labour-market and socialprotection support through post-crisis adjustment.

title: Le Chatelier with an Adjustable Constraint
affiliations: Renmin University of China

detail.title: Le Chatelier with an Adjustable Constraint

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The Le Chatelier principle says that a response computed with an auxiliary margin held fixed is smaller than the response that allows it to adjust. The classical statements assume the shock enters only the direct margin. When it enters both, that conclusion can fail, and it can fail in two distinct ways. This note gives necessary and sufficient conditions. For a smooth two-control problem with a positive-definite Hessian, let A and E be the own curvatures of the direct action and the adjustment, N their cross-partial, and p and r the direct effects of the shock on the two first-order conditions. Allowing adjustment yields a nonnegative response no larger than the fixed-margin response if and only if Nr ≤ Ep and Np ≤ Ar. If the first fails the response reverses sign; if the second fails while the first holds, adjustment magnifies rather than attenuates. The classical case is exactly r = 0, where the ratio of the two responses is AE/(AE − N²) ≥ 1 and magnification is universal. Attenuation is therefore possible only when the shock also moves the adjustment margin, which is the empirically common case.

title: Why did the EU roll back its corporate sustainability regulatory framework? Geopoliticization, stakeholder groups, and the shifting competitiveness discourse

detail.abstract: Over the decade following 2014, the EU introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework on corporate sustainability. However, a recent revision of the regulatory framework, the Omnibus I directive, substantially narrowed the framework’s scope and requirements. Why did this regulatory rollback occur? Theoretically, this paper adopts an explanatory framework that combines pressures from the global political economy context, the coalitional underpinnings of policy change, and a focus on discursive legitimization. Methodologically, it analyzes the official documents of EU institutions and key stakeholders, triangulated with semi-structured expert interviews. This paper argues that the regulatory rollback cannot be explained solely by business lobbying and power, nor can it be reduced to previous failed attempts to introduce sustainability reporting. Rather, a changed global political and economic context led to a geopoliticization of the framework, prompting the EU to revise its approach to corporate sustainability and providing an opening for key stakeholders to advocate successfully for policy change. The European Commission, in turn, articulated the notion of competitiveness to legitimize the regulatory rollback and build consensus around it, marking a destabilization of the previously dominant win-win articulation between corporate sustainability and competitiveness.

detail.abstract: Interdisciplinary governance research often relies on evidence dispersed across specialist databases, institutional repositories, legal portals, project websites, and publisher platforms. Researchers without comprehensive institutional database access face a methodological problem: they must produce a transparent and defensible evidence base without implying an exhaustiveness that the available infrastructure cannot support. This article develops a practical framework for resource-constrained evidence mapping in interdisciplinary European Union governance research. It distinguishes systematic core searching from supplementary web discovery, metadata-level screening from full-text assessment, bibliographic provenance from synthesis eligibility, and non-retrieval from substantive exclusion. The framework further requires separate reporting of search streams that cannot be reliably deduplicated, stable record identifiers, explicit decision statuses, access-path documentation, and non-compensatory consistency checks. An applied methodological illustration from research on European climate, education, culture, and participation governance demonstrates the logic. A reconstructed audit of 297 records yielded 182 confirmed metadata-level exclusions, 114 reopened full-text candidates, and one uncertain case. The prioritised set of 115 records was divided into 45 fully assessed texts and 70 records without complete full-text assessment. The 45 assessed texts were independently classifiable by evidence function and by access route, while a separate set of 149 historical candidates was retained solely as a bibliographic provenance set. The article argues that reproducibility under constrained access should be understood as transparent reconstruction of decisions, limits, and evidence functions rather than as a binary claim of database completeness. The proposed framework is relevant to scholars conducting documentintensive policy research with heterogeneous sources and uneven access conditions.

title: Negative Evidence in Qualitative Policy Document Analysis - A Status-Sensitive Framework for Claims about Absence, Silence, and Institutionalisation
