keywords: qualitative document analysis; negative evidence; policy analysis; institutionalisation; coding; absence claims; governance research

detail.abstract: Qualitative policy document analysis frequently relies on statements that a procedure, mandate, safeguard, or accountability mechanism is "absent" from an institutional arrangement. Such claims are methodologically demanding. Silence in one document may reflect document purpose, division of responsibility, incomplete source coverage, or an earlier policy version rather than genuine institutional absence. This article develops a status-sensitive framework for analysing negative evidence in legal, policy, programme, evaluation, and operational documents. The framework separates applicability, corpus sufficiency, textual evidence status, and degree of institutionalisation. It proposes a seven-value ordinal status system-0, X, 1, 2, 3, U, and N/Athat distinguishes non-documentation from explicit exclusion, programmatic recognition, procedural specification, assigned and reviewable responsibility, uncertainty, and nonapplicability. A six-step coding protocol is introduced for defining the expected institutional feature, identifying the relevant document family, testing applicability, coding evidence status, resolving contradictions, and formulating appropriately bounded claims. A worked example demonstrates why "not documented" must not be reported as "does not exist" and why selfdescriptions, legal acts, operational guidance, and evaluations carry different evidentiary weight. The article argues that negative-evidence claims should be treated as conditional inferences tied to a specified corpus and date. This approach improves transparency, reduces false deficit diagnoses, and supports more defensible comparison of policy instruments across sectors and levels of governance.

title: Who Drives the U.S. Treasury Premium?
affiliations: University of Basel

detail.title: Who Drives the U.S. Treasury Premium?
detail.abstract: I develop a model of sovereign portfolio choice with sector-specific U.S. Treasury preferences and estimate it on a new quarterly panel of Treasury holdings across countries and sectors. The estimates point to Treasury inconvenience: preferences beyond Treasuries' risk-return profile raise the return every investor requires, and the model-implied premium averages-77 basis points over 2013-2025. An investor's contribution to the premium depends not on its holdings alone but on how far Treasury preferences alter its demand elasticity. Domestic and foreign non-bank financial institutions and the foreign official sector, chiefly China, account for over two-thirds of it. U.S. debt sustainability is thus exposed both to geopolitical realignment abroad and to return-sensitive investors at home.

detail.abstract: Background and objective: Heart sound segmentation is a critical prerequisite for automated phonocardiogram (PCG) analysis and computer-aided diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. Existing methods generally adopt static fusion strategies for multi-source feature processing, which struggle to adapt to the non-stationary nature of heart sound signals and time-varying noise interference in real-world acquisition environments. Methods: To address this problem, we propose GADF-MBNet, a time-step-aware gated attention dynamic fusion network. The network employs a four-branch parallel architecture to extract four complementary feature types, including time-domain envelopes, time-frequency spectrograms, Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC), and cluster supervectors (CS). A gated attention unit computes adaptive fusion weights at each time step, while a multi-head self-attention mechanism captures long-range dependencies across cardiac cycles. Results: On the PhysioNet 2016 challenge dataset and the Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) clinical dataset, the proposed method achieves overall F1 scores of 98.29% and 95.59%, respectively, outperforming existing mainstream approaches. Ablation studies show that the dynamic fusion mechanism yields a larger gain on the more challenging MGH dataset, suggesting that adaptive weight allocation contributes to improved model robustness under diverse real-world recording conditions. Conclusions: The proposed architecture improves both segmentation accuracy and robustness to recording variability, supporting clinical translation of intelligent auscultation technology for cardiovascular diseases.

detail.abstract: Economic headroom is commonly evaluated at an individual position while prices, collateral values, regulatory rules, and other agents' actions are held fixed. That private or partial-equilibrium calculation can be informative, but it need not survive market clearing. This paper develops a general-equilibrium formulation in which current positions and consequential boundaries are jointly determined with prices, collateral values, regulation, and strategic responses. It defines private headroom, general-equilibrium headroom, the private-to-equilibrium wedge, an equilibrium-safe set, and systemic constraint. A central fixed-point theorem gives existence, uniqueness, continuity, and local comparative statics under transparent conditions. In a linearized loss system, the resolvent (I−A)⁻¹ maps a direct headroom loss into its equilibrium counterpart. This yields a precise condition under which positive private headroom disappears after feedback. A collateral-price specialization separates boundary activation, portfolio overlap, price impact, and regulatory adjustment. Further results show why averages of individual headroom do not determine systemic safety, how countercyclical boundary adjustment may reduce feedback under stated order conditions, and why privately protective actions need not be welfare improving. The framework's quantities are then computed from holdings under declared impact, liquidation and boundary calibrations. On complete semiannual holdings for Chinese equity and hybrid mutual funds over ten half-years, the spectral radius of the amplification operator ends 11 per cent above its starting value, after peaking in 2023 rather than rising steadily, and the stability margin narrows by about a tenth; between 20 and 2,779 funds are privately safe and equilibrium-breached in the calibrated scenarios. A fund's exposure to what others crowd into predicts its subsequent de-risking; membership of the breached set, once ordinary drawdown is controlled for, does not, and both halves are reported. The mathematical ingredients are established fixed-point, comparative-static, and network tools. The narrower contribution is to organize them around equilibrium-consistent consequential boundaries and to state the claim restrictions required for empirical use. The paper does not provide new causal evidence.

detail.abstract: This paper develops the static and dynamic foundations of bilateral equilibrium in two-sided exchange. Our main result identifies acyclicity of the improvement graph, together with global compatibility, as a central structural condition supporting bilateral equilibrium existence and decentralized stability. Acyclicity therefore provides a structural compatibility condition connecting local pairwise efficiency with market-wide bilateral stability. We then study how decentralized economies adjust toward these equilibria. We introduce deterministic and stochastic bilateral-improvement dynamics in which agents myopically adopt profitable bilateral deviations. Under acyclicity, the induced bilateral-improvement relation over efficient contracts admits a numerical representation: a welfare potential that strictly increases along every profitable deviation. This potential is a global Lyapunov function, ruling out improvement cycles and ensuring that every deterministic improvement path converges in finite time to a bilateral equilibrium. When deviations occur with logit-perturbed choice, the resulting perturbed Markov process is aperiodic. If the transition structure is irreducible, then the process admits a unique stationary distribution. Using Young's resistance-tree framework, we show that welfare-increasing deviations have zero resistance, while welfare-decreasing moves have resistance equal to the welfare drop. Under the perturbed dynamics, welfare-maximizing acyclic equilibria receive positive limiting probability as noise vanishes. Taken together, these results unify existence, welfare, deterministic convergence, and stochastic selection in bilateral exchange. Acyclicity, together with global compatibility, emerges as a central structural condition linking static stability with dynamic adjustment and long-run equilibrium selection.

detail.abstract: Motivated by the long swings in the U.S. price-rent ratio, this paper allows its longrun benchmark to shift within the present-value framework, following Lettau and Van Nieuwerburgh (2008). detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence and data systems become more involved in destination management, tourism professionals may need competencies that extend beyond operating digital tools. This exploratory paper develops a provisional framework for examining these requirements from a vocational education perspective. A selective conceptual synthesis of literature on smart tourism, automation, governance, and digital education informs five candidate domains: digital and analytical literacy; AI interpretation and supervision; human-machine collaboration; ethical and governance judgment; and adaptive and relational learning. These domains are working categories rather than empirically established dimensions. We use autonomous destination governance as a bounded concept describing increasing delegation of selected management functions to algorithmic systems under institutional and human oversight. The paper then proposes a small qualitative pre-test to examine whether practitioners and educators recognise the categories, understand their boundaries, and can relate them to concrete tasks. No primary data have been collected for this paper. Its contribution is a starting framework and an empirical development route for a larger study of tourism workforce competencies and curriculum needs.

detail.abstract: I model a global coordination game between a state-sponsored attacker targeting critical financial market infrastructure (FMI), such as SWIFT, and a continuum of foreign investors whose sudden capital reversals trigger exchange market pressure. I empirically test the resulting theoretical propositions using a Double Machine Learning Local Projections framework on a panel of 30 emerging markets from 2015 to 2024. Results reveal a severe nonlinear macro-financial vulnerability. I demonstrate that moderate FMI cyber attacks are smoothly absorbed by institutional buffers and redundant backup systems; under these conditions, foreign investors default to rational inattention and hold their positions, resulting in no significant exchange market response. In contrast, extreme tail-risk FMI cyber attacks (99th percentile) overwhelm this resilience and trigger a panicked first-mover advantage dynamic. Fearing institutional liquidity freezes, foreign investors rapidly liquidate emerging market exposure, generating an immediate surge in exchange market pressure. This asymmetric flight-to-safety actively fractures emerging market integration as capital retreats to core-market safe havens. Ultimately, these findings establish that emerging markets are structurally forced to absorb the macroeconomic fallout of FMI cyber shocks, severely exacerbating cross-border financial fragmentation and contagion.

detail.abstract: This article explores the concept of loyalty, particularly in the context of the military. In that context, loyalty is generally seen as a virtue. Outside that context, most ethicists see loyalty as a "gray" virtue at best. And not without reason: the fact that most militaries tend to stress loyalty is a cause of both unethical behavior and the cover-ups following incidents. For a better understanding of the mechanisms behind such incidents, it is helpful to distinguish between loyalty to a group and loyalty to principles such as justice, as it is only the former that leads to unethical behavior and cover-ups. Regrettably, most militaries define loyalty as loyalty to the organization and colleagues. This article suggests that militaries could promote loyalty to the military profession as a feasible middle ground between morally questionable group loyalty and the perhaps too-hard-to-attain loyalty to principle.

detail.abstract: Multi-stakeholder drafting of laws and regulations is praised for bringing diverse perspectives into the drafting process. However, it frequently leaves the meaning and implications of key legal concepts insufficiently specified, and not as a deliberate use of vagueness. Drawing on the EU AI Act's Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment regime and the US Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act, we illustrate how multistakeholder drafting can defer conceptual choices, creating costs for the interpretation and implementation of law. We propose a new experimental method, inspired by regulatory sandboxes, to address this problem before laws or regulations are enacted: conceptual sandboxes. A conceptual sandbox is a pre-codification controlled environment where lawmakers and stakeholders test and compare candidate concepts alongside the norms and institutional arrangements by which they operate. Combining conceptual engineering with methods from software and requirements engineering, we specify a six-phase protocol that maps contested concepts, predicts the effects of enacting them, stress-tests those predictions, compares alternatives, re-engineers the concept, and audits the result after enactment. A counterfactual application of the original Article 27 of the AI Act illustrates how the protocol can expose weaknesses in legal design before enactment.

detail.abstract: Governments that recruit scientists also hold powers to interrupt a researcher's career or to stop a researcher leaving the country. This article asks how that combination affects competition for scientific capacity, and it answers by treating recruitment in the United States and China as a problem of credible commitment. A scientist who moves makes investments whose value depends on continuity of status, meaning continued permission to do the work, and on freedom to leave. A change to either can cut the value of an appointment once the move is made. American litigation in 2025 and 2026 shows the executive changing these conditions and the courts limiting the changes. China recruits abroad while restricting the exit of defined groups, and a decree in force since September 2026 adds a ground based on industrial and technological security. Published studies of scientific mobility document costs from political pressure on researchers, and the recruitment effects of these legal rules have yet to be measured. Procedural safeguards can strengthen recruitment where researchers make large investments tied to one destination and have credible alternatives elsewhere, though the outcome also turns on funding and institutional quality, and on the researcher's citizenship. The article proposes domestic protection for continuity of status and timely review of security decisions, coordinated through existing international instruments.

detail.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly pair economic offers with response windows: prices, pickup slots, promotions, and service quotes expire if customers do not act in time. This paper studies how a seller should learn prices and deadlines when the deadline itself determines which demand outcomes are observed. After observing a customer context, the seller chooses both a price and a finite purchase deadline. Customers have a latent valuation and an action-dependent consideration delay. The purchase outcome is observed only if the decision arrives before the deadline, while expired offers leave the latent buy-reject outcome censored. This creates endogenous censoring: the seller controls both the economic terms of the offer and the observation window through which demand is learned. We formulate a contextual price-deadline learning model with open-offer costs and propose Contextual Optimization of Pricing and Deadlining with Exploration (COPDE). The algorithm separates timing learning from demand learning, uses inverse-probability and exposure-normalized updates to recover latent demand from deadline-censored feedback, and deploys an optimistic elimination strategy to dynamically pair prices with optimal deadlines. We prove that COPDE achieves regret O (𝑇^2/3) and show that this rate is optimal in 𝑇 on a natural pricing subclass. The model identifies conditions under which shorter deadlines increase conversion while reducing holding costs, and shows why identical conversion rates can conceal different optimal deadlines. Numerical experiments evaluate learning performance against fixed-deadline and explore-then-commit benchmarks, examine sensitivity to the timing model, and show how higher holding costs can favor longer deadlines when lower prices accelerate customer response.

detail.abstract: Iran cannot outlast the blockade, the sanctions and the recurring strikes: losses that depend on imports persist under blockade, and repairs Iran can make at home must be struck again. Tehran's position therefore worsens each month for three assets: export revenue, import-dependent plant and the credibility of its missile force. For those assets a settlement now is worth more to Iran than a later one. The claim does not reach oil in the ground, which largely returns on relief, though the gas reinjection Iran's mature fields need is cut further the longer the blockade holds. It does not reach the enriched uranium, whose value to Tehran may rise. The United States' legal position is strongest when it answers Iranian fire. Strikes on rebuilding that no Iranian attack precedes rest on the executive's own reading, which no court or international body has endorsed. Four limits hold: the campaign contains Iran and does not remove its government, so it does not deliver regime change; the enriched uranium remains unaccounted for; the compounding of losses rests on a single measured recovery interval, in the asset class where it is weakest, and SP-2 tests it (Section 9); and no settlement lasts unless Washington makes its offer of relief credible, which requires a public commitment to the survival of the Iranian state as a settlement term (Section 8).

detail.abstract: Martingales sit at the centre of derivative pricing, stochastic modelling, measure changes and quantitative model validation, yet they are often recognized through incomplete shortcuts. This first article in a three-part series develops a practical threeroute framework: direct conditional expectation, inspection of the finite-variation term in an Itô decomposition, and the square-integrable Brownian stochastic-integral theorem. It separates true martingales from local martingales and applies the framework to Brownian motion, squared Brownian motion and compensated squared Brownian motion. The examples show why a flat simulated mean does not establish a martingale and why zero Itô drift initially yields only a local-martingale conclusion. The central message is practical: the probability measure, filtration and integrability argument must be made explicit before a martingale claim is used in pricing or model validation.

detail.abstract: Stochastic exponentials connect compensation, change of measure and risk-neutral pricing, but zero drift alone normally establishes only a local martingale. The results show that simulation can reveal coding, compensation and discretization errors but cannot replace filtration-aware proof and integrability conditions. detail.abstract: Nigeria now measures poverty better than ever before. The 2022 national Multidimensional Poverty Index found that 133 million people, 63 per cent of the population, were multidimensionally poor, and that 65 per cent of them lived in the North. Yet better counting has not produced better reaching. This article argues that poverty measures, even multidimensional ones, often miss the social relations that make some people poorer than others, especially gender. Drawing on the poverty and gender units of two Development Studies courses at the National Open University of Nigeria, on their authors research on immunisation, polio eradication and social analysis in health programmes, and on joint research on gendered environmental knowledge, the article identifies three blind spots in how poverty is understood and addressed in northern Nigeria: health, where children who are never reached by services remain invisible; energy, where the burden of cooking fuel falls mainly on women; and knowledge, where women's understanding of their own environment and livelihoods is rarely treated as evidence. The article concludes that reaching the poor requires not only better data but social analysis of who is missed and why, and that the education of girls and the voice of women are central to both.

detail.abstract: This article proposes the development of collective human intelligence (CHI) as a response to concerns about artificial intelligence and the limited capacity of political organisations to address growing societal complexity. We examine how a variable organisational structure-the dynamic networkcould enable party subdivisions to combine distributed knowledge, develop shared decisions and coordinate their implementation. The method involves orderly transitions between sectoral groups and cross-groups, followed by collective adoption of decisions and implementation through dedicated groups. We hypothesise that organising interaction in this way can limit the escalation of conflicts used to establish personal dominance, support trust and create conditions for mutual learning. Repeated cycles of deliberation, joint action and evaluation may strengthen collective intelligence and organisational agency. AI serves as a supporting tool, with its proposals subject to expert scrutiny and collective discussion, while responsibility remains with people. Experience from more than 170 documented events provides a practical basis for exploring the approach, although the sustained development of CHI through repeated cycles remains a hypothesis requiring further testing. While the article focuses on political parties, the approach could also be applied in civil society organisations and think tanks.

detail.abstract: This article examines the extent to which direct digital connectivity between Brazil and Portugal contributes to the strategic autonomy of both countries in the South Atlantic. It studies the EllaLink system, including the Fortaleza-Sines connection, as an empirical case without equating physical infrastructure with state control or digital sovereignty. The article argues that a direct transatlantic route can reduce specific geographic dependencies and expand channels for scientific, educational, and economic cooperation, but it does not create full strategic autonomy. The corridor remains embedded in transnational chains of finance, technology, operation, maintenance, regulation, and interconnection. The analysis distinguishes among connectivity, resilience, and autonomy, and combines a qualitative case study, documentary analysis, and exploratory process tracing. The evidence indicates that the strategic value of the infrastructure depends less on the cable's existence in isolation than on the ability of Brazil and Portugal to diversify routes, identify dependencies, coordinate regulators, and establish mechanisms for prevention, repair, and service continuity. The conclusion is therefore conditional: the connection enlarges the two countries' room for manoeuvre in specific geographic and institutional dimensions while preserving significant technological, corporate, financial, operational, and regulatory dependencies.

detail.abstract: This scholarly paper examines the constitutional status of "hate speech" and the recurring argument that expression capable of inflicting serious individual and social harms should therefore be subject to legal prohibition. Written in the unconventional form of verse, but grounded in First Amendment doctrine and legal scholarship, the paper contributes to the literature by separating two questions that are too often conflated: whether hateful expression can cause genuine harm, and whether government should possess the power to suppress it. Accepting the substantial harms that racist, demeaning, and intolerant expression can inflict, the paper nevertheless argues that those harms do not establish a constitutionally workable category of prohibited "hate speech." Drawing principally on Matal v. Tam and the Supreme Court's broader jurisprudence protecting offensive and disfavored expression, the paper identifies three central difficulties with hate speech regulation. These are the indeterminacy of "hate speech" as a legal category, the First Amendment prohibition against governmental viewpoint discrimination, and the danger that censorship powers created to suppress despised speakers will ultimately be deployed against dissenters and marginalized groups themselves. The paper ultimately defends a distinction fundamental to the American free speech tradition, which is that expression may be hateful without being unlawful. That is, just because speech is of forceful social condemnation does not make it a proper object of state censorship.

detail.abstract: In 2019, the author's MIST report assessed DNA as a candidate medium for archival data storage. This paper revisits that assessment seven years later, and it is the first application of the vertical market failure (VMF) framework to a specific storage technology. The physics of DNA storage are confirmed and the science has advanced. Enzymatic synthesis, read-side coding, and interoperability standards developed by the DNA Data Storage Alliance all show real progress. Commercial viability nonetheless remains years away. Write throughput is still measured in megabytes per day, while magnetic tape writes hundreds of megabytes per second, and synthesis costs remain orders of magnitude from hyperscale economics. The paper argues that the limiting factor is the capital structure, not the science. Incumbent storage suppliers have little incentive to fund a substitute. Hyperscale buyers have no mechanism for direct investment in pre-competitive research. Venture capital has proven insufficient in scale and patience. With the first generation of commercial ventures consolidated or acquired, the burden shifted to public and institutional capital. The field now holds the evidence and the coordination capacity to make a credible case for that capital.

detail.abstract: This study examines commodity tail dependence and exchange-rate risk in Ghana using two co-equal calendar constructions for cocoa, gold, Brent crude oil, WTI crude oil and the Ghanaian cedi over 2015-2026. detail.abstract: New Keynesian models predict stronger real effects of monetary policy when prices are stickier. We provide the first empirical evidence linking local price stickiness to monetary transmission, identifying a distinct source of geographic heterogeneity.

title: The Jurisdictional Independence Thesis: A Formal, Probabilistic, and Empirical Analysis of Omittoism and of Why Creation, Power, Knowledge, and Perfection Do Not Generate a Right to Rule
affiliations: Monash University

detail.title: The Jurisdictional Independence Thesis: A Formal, Probabilistic, and Empirical Analysis of Omittoism and of Why Creation, Power, Knowledge, and Perfection Do Not Generate a Right to Rule

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationship has influenced the study. It was a self-funded research.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded research

detail.abstract: Debates in the philosophy of religion are organised around whether a creator exists. Omittoism relocates a logically prior question: by what right would any being, whatever its power or origin, issue binding commands to autonomous agents? This paper reconstructs Omittoism as a formal and empirically testable research programme. We state its core as the Jurisdictional Independence Thesis (JIT) and decompose it into a grounding principle and an origin-exclusion principle; we classify fourteen candidate "legitimacy generators" and show, by considered-judgment cases and a superlative-parity argument, that none of creation, sustenance, power, knowledge or goodness suffices without a further bridge premise; we prove an ontological-invariance theorem and give a formal version of the Juridical Cleavage against Thomistic replies; we derive, in a Bayesian model of revelation, an explicit reliability threshold π * below which even a morally perfect commander lacks Razian authority, and illustrate it with global religiouscomposition data; we show by repeated-game analysis that jurisdictional sovereignty is compatible with sustained cooperation while exposing the limits of pure consent, which forces a repair of the framework's original third axiom; we prove that existential dependence does not entail normative subordination, resolve a jurisdictional Euthyphro trilemma, show that supremacy is not unlimited domain, and stress-test the framework on ten institutional and seven counterfactual cases after reconstructing the strongest theistic case; we assemble the results into a pro tanto Divine Jurisdiction Thesis; and we derive falsifiable predictions, with a simulation-based power analysis, and explicit defeat conditions. The surviving core of Omittoism is a non-entailment and burden-shifting result, not a refutation of divine authority; we specify exactly what would overturn it.

detail.abstract: The metaphor of society as a neural network is not new. Prior research has modeled human society using neural-network and Boltzmann-machine analogies, while newer work on society-in-the-loop governance, institutional AI, human-AI coordination, and AI-orchestrated organizations has moved toward socio-technical systems in which artificial agents participate in collective action. This paper therefore does not claim priority for the metaphor. It defines a narrower and testable architecture: the Societal Neural Network (SocNN), a heterogeneous coordination network in which human actors, AI agents, and institutional actors can receive, delegate, execute, constrain, and learn from work under explicit authority and governance conditions. The minimum operational mechanism is termed a Governed Adaptive Coordination Network (GACN). A GACN couples capability representation, authority-aware routing, execution provenance, outcome evidence, adaptive routing, and governance constraints. Its key design rule is non-self-escalation: performance feedback may change capability confidence and routing preferences, but it cannot by itself expand an actor's authority. The paper formalizes SocNN as a stateful coordination system, specifies necessary conditions that distinguish it from social-network metaphors, conventional multi-agent systems, workflow orchestration, and governance frameworks, and derives six falsifiable propositions. It then proposes a replay-and-field-test design comparing manual, rule-based, capability-only, and governance-aware adaptive routing. The intended contribution is a research object that connects organization theory, multi-agent systems, AI governance, and computational social systems without collapsing governance into optimization or treating institutions as passive context.

detail.title: Loss Aversion and Interim Feedback in Tournaments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how reference-dependent preferences affect effort incentives in a tournament with interim performance feedback. Feedback typically weakens effort incentives by revealing a performance gap and reducing the marginal effect of effort on the probability of winning. We show that this effect depends critically on an agent's interim position. Reference-dependent preferences strengthen the effort incentive of the leading agent but weaken that of the lagging agent. When only the leader has reference-dependent preferences, the additional incentive generated by loss aversion can be sufficiently strong to overturn the usual discouragement effect of feedback, so that both the leader's effort and total effort exceed the no-feedback benchmark. Our analysis thus provides a theoretical explanation for the observed possibility that interim performance feedback can increase rather than decrease effort in competitive environments.

detail.abstract: This paper examines Kuwait Decree-Law No. 89 of 2025, which amended Law No. 118 of 2023 concerning the establishment and economic development of residential cities and areas. The reform is treated as more than a technical amendment to housing legislation. It creates a more flexible legal architecture for structuring project companies, calibrating public financial participation through feasibility studies, diversifying housing products, integrating residential and non-residential uses, and applying the framework to selected existing cities and public lands. The paper argues that these changes can assist Kuwait in moving from a predominantly direct public-delivery model toward a regulated development ecosystem in which the State remains responsible for planning, land allocation, standards, supervision and the social objectives of housing welfare, while private developers contribute capital, expertise, construction capacity and lifecycle management. The analysis situates the reform within Kuwait's housing demand, emerging real estate developer procurements and Vision 2035. It also identifies the conditions that determine whether the positive potential is realised in practice: competitive procurement, rigorous feasibility analysis, disciplined risk allocation, affordability safeguards, consumer protection and credible long-term contract management.

title: A Dedicated Retail Tariff for Energy Communities -Mitigating the Grid Cost Death Spiral?
affiliations: University College Dublin (UCD), Ruhr University of Bochum and Ruhr-University Bochum

detail.title: A Dedicated Retail Tariff for Energy Communities -Mitigating the Grid Cost Death Spiral?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest in this work.
declarations.funderStatement: M.T.Devine acknowledges funding from Research Ireland and co-funding partners under grant number 21/SPP/3756 through the NexSys Strategic Partnership Programme. This work is also related to research carried out in the context of the REFRAME project (“DecentRalization of Electricity Systems– An Integrated Approach For Risk Assessment and Mitigation in the Energy Sector”). SJ and VB acknowledge funding by the Deutsche Forschungs gemeinschaft (DFG) under grant number 548388828.

detail.abstract: Energy communities typically face volumetric retail tariffs, where self-consumption reduces their contribution to fixed grid costs. This tariff design incentivises investments in prosumer technologies. Yet, the resulting decrease in grid demand leads to increasing (volumetric) grid charges, which shifts the burden of grid costs to remaining consumers and causes a grid cost death spiral. We propose a novel retail tariff design that mitigates this dynamic while preserving investment incentives: the share of grid costs to be recovered from energy communities is based on their pre-prosumer reference demand, keeping their total cost burden constant as self-consumption increases. We compare this tariff to the status-quo uniform tariff, each with four different shares of volumetric vs. fixed grid cost components. We apply a stochastic equilibrium model of the Irish electricity market solved iteratively over 25 investment periods, capturing dynamic feedback between prosumer and generator decisions. The model encompasses generating firms with varying market power and different consumer groups, including four energy communities. Under the proposed energy community tariff, investments in solar PV and batteries exceed those under the uniform status-quo tariff, while non-investing consumers are shielded from rising retail premia. They additionally benefit from positive externalities from prosumer investments as emissions and wholesale market prices decline, decreasing excess firm profits, particularly when market power is present. All consumers' costs decrease for moderate volumetric cost shares between 50% and 75%. The proposed tariff design thus reconciles cost-reflectivity with decentralised renewable investment incentives, offering a practical instrument to address the grid cost death spiral.

affiliations: University of Colorado at Boulder - Department of Economics

affiliations.org_name: University of Colorado at Boulder - Department of Economics

detail.abstract: Arms control is rare, and military spending keeps rising. This paper treats world peace as a public good whose value standard willingness-to-pay measures understate, and military spending as an input that domestic interests and the security dilemma push beyond efficient levels. It proposes a Coase-like institution from which every participating nation gains. Nations make fixed contributions to a Peace Fund and pledge ceilings on audited military spending. Ceilings below a historical baseline are paid for annually in proportion to the reduction, ceilings above it are charged at the same rate, and breaking a pledge, including by covertly supporting proxy forces, forfeits payment and incurs a bonded liability. In a contest model, paying fifty cents per dollar of reduction cuts arming by a third while returning each nation's contribution. Calibrated to the United States and China, combined savings are about $430 billion a year with relative strength unchanged.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how high school bullying and discrimination are associated with mental distress, both during high school and later in life. Using retrospective data from adults in Australia, we document the reported frequency of past bullying and whether, during their time in high school, respondents experienced discrimination based on characteristics such as ethnicity, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender, or physical appearance. Frequent bullying is particularly prevalent among certain groups and is most common among those targeted due to a disability. We find that bullying is strongly associated with greater mental distress during high school, which persists into adulthood, even after accounting for experiences of discrimination. These associations are strongest for frequent bullying and are observed for both men and women. Discrimination based on disability and sexual orientation is also independently associated with greater mental distress. The findings underscore the significant challenges faced by those who experience frequent bullying during their teenage years, particularly among groups already experiencing discrimination.

detail.abstract: This article examines how financial factors are associated with the likelihood of obtaining independent validation of climate targets and whether such validation is associated with lower corporate carbon emissions. Using the Covid-19 crisis as an exogenous shock to firms' financial constraints and investment capacity, I analyze 1,852 publicly listed firms from 2015-2024. I find that financial performance and cash holdings increase the probability of obtaining independent validation, while R&D spending and dividend distributions reduce it. I also find a negative association between SBTi validation and indirect carbon emissions. However, the empirical scope of this association remains limited.

detail.abstract: This paper aims to provide an empirical, post-implementation evaluation of the trade effects of the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). By focusing on the sectoral limitations of the CBAM coverage, the paper provides a difference-in-differences (DiD) analysis, by using monthly bilateral trade data from January 2016 to August 2026 for twenty non-EU exporter economies and six destination markets. First of all, the findings show that after the start of the transitioning period of the CBAM in October 2023, the export of the downstream products proposed for the 2028 CBAM Expansion has significantly increased comparing to the control group. Second specification uses triple differences (DDD) and shows that this increase is concentrated towards the non-EU destination markets. The export of downstream products to the European market has barely changed, whereas there is a statistically significant increase in the exports of the same product group to non-EU markets, proving the trade diversion in anticipation of future CBAM expansion and obligations. The results are robust with respect to five robustness checks. Finally, the event study shows two clear shifts in 2021-Q3 and 2023-Q4, and no significant evidence of a parallel trend before these periods.

detail.abstract: This paper presents an open-source electric capacity-expansion model of Colorado. Few models exist that align with state jurisdictions because the electric industry is made up of utilities, markets, and balancing authorities whose footprints often do not align with state borders. This model is organized around Colorado's political boundary to provide insight on questions relevant to state policymakers and regulators. It is a multi-period, least-cost optimization of the electricity system representing new investment, operations, in-state transmission limits, resource adequacy, and state-level carbon reduction policy. The model is implemented with the PyPSA and HiGHS software. It is demonstrated through a reference case, a comparison with no carbon policy, a case isolating the state from regional electricity trade, and a sensitivity that relaxes internal transmission limits. Results show that, under this paper's technology cost and load growth assumptions, the cost of state carbon policy is concentrated almost entirely in the final few percentage points to reach 100% reduction. Furthermore, building and operating a system with no or limited regional trade is significantly more expensive than a reference system. The transmission sensitivity shows existing in-state transmission capacity limits new wind development in the state's windiest East region to about 2.9 GW above existing wind, with further wind built in the North region that has lower wind quality but better connectivity to load. Promising areas for future work and development are discussed. The model and underlying data are released publicly for reuse and extension.

detail.abstract: We construct city-level measures of freeway disamenities and examine their association with metropolitan growth. We combine neighborhood-level estimates from Brinkman and Lin (2024) with calibrated spatial models for U.S. metropolitan areas. Each city measure is based on a counterfactual that removes estimated disamenities while holding modeled travel times fixed. Cities with larger estimated disamenities grew more slowly, conditioned on total freeway mileage and initial population. Total freeway mileage is positively associated with growth in the same specification. Estimated disamenities are larger in cities with greater 1950 populations, more centralized freeway networks, and coastal geography. These patterns are consistent with local quality-of-life costs attenuating regional accessrelated growth benefits.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NO.

detail.abstract: Invalid ballots are votes that cost the voter time and effort but are not counted, yet ballot-level evidence from Iraq and the Kurdistan Region is scarce. In Duhok Governorate, 5.55% of the ballots cast in the 2025 parliamentary election were invalid, slightly below the reported national share of about 6%. This study asks how these ballots are distributed across marking patterns and registration centers, and what a bounded rationality perspective can and cannot say about them. All 34,694 invalid ballots were classified from scanned images into seven patterns following the criteria of the Independent High Electoral Commission. The classification was carried out under the supervision of the author with five trainers of the same electoral office, and results are summarized with frequencies, percentages, and the minimum, median, and maximum share of each pattern across centers; no inferential tests are applied. Overvotes dominate: ballots marking three or more lists account for 42.00% of invalid ballots and those marking two lists for 39.38%, followed by blank ballots (7.96%), candidate number without a list (6.37%), marks outside the range (2.79%), marks between two lists (1.12%), and marks with a different pen (0.38%). Composition varies widely across the 41 registration centers, with the share of three-or-more-list ballots ranging from 0% to 72.76%, and an abrupt break between the first five centers and the rest cannot be separated from differences in classification. The patterns are heterogeneous, and the data cannot distinguish procedural error from protest. The results suggest that ballot format and voting instructions are a natural focus for further study. The findings are limited to one election in one governorate, contain no information on voter intent, and rely on internal coding.

detail.abstract: We demonstrate the impacts of climate change-driven temperature increases on building energy consumption in New York City. Combining building-level monthly electricity and gas disclosures with high spatial-and temporal-resolution weather data and downscaled climate projections, we estimate heterogeneous energy demand responses to heating and cooling degree hours, and use the resulting fitted empirical models to project warming effects on energy consumption circa 2050. Summer cooling electricity increases substantially (up to 19%), but is offset by reduced gas consumption for heating in winter and shoulder seasons (up to 7%), for a 0.08% to 0.98% net annual impact depending on the warming scenario, resulting in between 40.04 and 53.28 thousand metric tons of corresponding CO2 savings at our sample scale (respectively).

detail.abstract: Two Indians were wounded when the LTTE attacked the Sri Lanka Air Force radar station at Vavuniya on 9 September 2008. Both governments described them as civilian engineers employed by Bharat Electronics. A 2019 Armed Forces Tribunal judgment shows that one of them, Chintamani Rout, was a serving Indian Air Force airman. He was deputed to Sri Lanka under Project Drishti as crew chief of No. 2 Air Defence Radar Squadron, and the Air Force later certified him a battle casualty. Drawing on that judgment, service citations, diplomatic cables and contemporary reporting, this article shows how India supplied INDRA-II radar systems, anti-aircraft weapons and military personnel. That support helped Sri Lanka neutralise the Tigers' nascent air wing and protect the bases sustaining its ground offensive. The article argues that India presented this operational military footprint as civilian or "non-lethal" assistance in order to preserve its regional influence while facing severe domestic backlash from Tamil Nadu, where protesters condemned their government's complicity in the war.

detail.abstract: This paper uses a panel dataset of gridded annual crop yields and investigates the global temperature, precipitation, carbon fertilization and irrigation responses of four crops responsible for 75% of world's calorie intake. Regression results give a consistent average approximation of yield saturating CO2 fertilization effect on grid-cell level yields ranging from 0.29% to 0.66% per 1 ppm CO2 - and exceeding yield gains from adjustments in irrigation. Projecting climatically-driven changes in crop yields, by combining our estimated responses over the period 2000-2015 with an ensemble of climate model mid-century simulations, we find substantial agreement among GCMs on average crop yield declines of <10% due to weather components and crop inclines of >20% due to CFE alone-with the largest effects on rice and spring wheat, under a vigorous warming scenario. Combining large CFE responses with elevated CO2 SSP forecasts shows that mid-century impacts of increasing temperatures on global calorie supply are systematically offset by CO2 fertilization.

title: What Does a Couple's Recorded Joint Position Represent? Intrahousehold Heterogeneity and Provenance in Financial Planning
affiliations: MN SAPIENS

detail.title: What Does a Couple's Recorded Joint Position Represent? Intrahousehold Heterogeneity and Provenance in Financial Planning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of MN SAPIENS, a professional practice that develops methods for documenting multi-participant family financial decisions. The author's practice has specified internal record requirements that include participant-specific source states, a recorded resolution basis and participant confirmation. Those internal requirements overlap with the provenance-oriented practice implication discussed in Section 7 of this paper. No MN SAPIENS product or method is described or evaluated in the paper, and the paper makes no effectiveness or uniqueness claim for those practices.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper is an integrative review and conceptual working paper using synthetic constructions. No human participants, client or family data, or case-study subjects were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract:
Financial-planning records can contain a single joint position for a couple: a household risk profile, a joint objective, a shared return expectation, or a statement of who decides. The provenance of that record is not self-evident. Spouses differ in preferences, beliefs and perceived financial knowledge; their influence over joint choices also varies and depends partly on who reports it. In a large client-record study, a gap between spouses' recorded risk tolerance is less likely to be observed when they attend the adviser together, although the association admits several explanations. CFP Board guidance for marital engagements treats each spouse as a client, while European suitability rules require an ex-ante policy for groups of natural persons and permit individual assessment of each client.

The question examined here is narrower than the established household-finance debate: what does a recorded joint position represent when its formation is not preserved? Evidence from collective household economics, within-couple disagreement and influence research, adviser-elicitation studies and professional standards is brought to bear on that question. A compact representation device, J = F(x_A, x_B, w, c, r), and three synthetic constructions show that materially different combinations of participant states, influence, elicitation context and resolution rule can yield the same recorded joint position. A bare J therefore leaves its evidential warrant uncertain: whose state it carries, how it was formed, and what divergence remained unresolved. Counter-evidence on portfolio outcomes and alternative readings of joint attendance are retained because the record claim does not depend on either effect being large. The practice implication is limited and unvalidated, and the author's earlier downstream handoff work is treated as prior art rather than as validation.

detail.abstract: This paper reviews evidence related to justice technology, focusing on what we know-and still need to know-about the role and importance of technology and technology policy in achieving people-centered justice. Over the past two decades, technology has emerged as a core focus of efforts to close the global justice gap. Despite significant investment in justice technology-ranging from data digitization and online dispute resolution to AI-powered legal tools-rigorous evaluation of whether these interventions achieve their intended outcomes remain scarce. This article surveys the existing research landscape across two domains: the justice technology stack, including data infrastructure and public-facing services, and the enabling environment required for justice technology to thrive, encompassing state capacity, funding models, and regulatory frameworks. While the literature documents considerable activity in user experience design, technology access, and AI governance, it largely fails to answer the fundamental question of whether justice technologies work for the people they are meant to serve. This contribution also identifies critical knowledge gaps across both domains-including the absence of agreed-upon impact metrics, systemic interoperability failures, inadequate cybersecurity research, and limited inquiry into procurement practices and public budgets-and proposes a research agenda to address them. It argues that closing these knowledge gaps is essential not only to improving justice technology outcomes, but to building the evidence needed to attract sustained investment, support credible policy reform, and ultimately advance a people-centered justice system.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the score test for spatially lagged regressors (W X) in SLX models when the data may also exhibit spatial dependence in the lagged dependent variable or the error term. Building on the exact score identity of Koley (2024), $S_{\rho} = S_{\lambda} + \hat{\beta}'_{nc} S_{\theta}$, we show that the unadjusted SLX score test admits an exact, sample-by-sample decomposition $RS_{\theta} = PS_{\theta} + OS_{\theta}$. $PS_{\theta}$ equals numerically, in every sample, the classical robust lag test $RS^*_{\rho}$ of Anselin et al. (1996); the orthogonal remainder $OS_{\theta}$, on k-2 degrees of freedom, is the only component orthogonal to the common-factor direction of Burridge (1981). It is asymptotically $\chi^2_{k-2}$ without normality and, under normality, has an exact finite-sample null law, a rescaled Beta with an equivalent F statistic at every $n$. $OS_{\theta}$ tests whether the lagged regressors enter only through the aggregated column $WX_{nc}\beta_{nc}$; non-rejection bounds, rather than rules out, spillovers along that direction. At k = 2 the remainder is undefined and the battery reduces to the classical tests. Across five cross-sections, the decomposition separates common-factor effects in Ertur-Koch, Columbus, and Georgia from covariate-specific spillovers in St. Louis and Baltimore.

detail.abstract: Is everything political? In academia, in activism and in public debate the affirmative answer has become a widely shared assumption, and questioning it is often taken as a defense of the established order. This article questions it while granting much of what motivates it. Nothing in social life is natural, power runs through the family, art and science, and any practice may one day become an object of struggle. It does not follow that everything is political. The central argument is that relation is not constitution. When a social practice influences politics, or when politics affects it, a causal bond is established between them, and that bond, even when it runs in both directions, leaves the internal logic of each intact. A practice affected by politics goes on reproducing itself according to its own rules, and it becomes political when a group publicly contests the rules that bind everyone. Everything else may bear the marks of power and still belong to those who live it. The aim of this delimitation is to give political theory and political practice a sharper concept of their object. Declaring everything political has a paradoxical effect. It depoliticizes, because it blurs the difference between being subject to power and having a part in its contestation, and it disperses the energy that social transformation needs to concentrate.

detail.abstract: In an April post, using millions of homeowners' insurance contracts matched with propertylevel exposure and disaster risk, we showed that although households are insured, they are still "on the hook" because deductibles and coverage limits leave homeowners responsible for part of a loss. Because insurers cannot perfectly observe how well homeowners maintain or protect their properties (a problem known as "moral hazard"), contract terms such as deductibles can play an important role in balancing risk sharing and incentives. By requiring homeowners to bear part of a loss, insurers can preserve incentives for policyholders to take actions that reduce damage risk. In this post, we quantify the cost of keeping homeowners on the hook. How costly is moral hazard in homeowner's insurance? How much risk must households retain to preserve these incentives? And, importantly, who ultimately bears that residual risk? The short answer is that keeping homeowners on the hook costs insurers relatively little, but it leaves households with substantial risk, especially those least able to absorb a large loss. How Do We Estimate Moral Hazard? We build and estimate a model of insurance contract design, drawing on the classic moralhazard framework of Holmström. Moral hazard is inherently difficult to measure because the underlying actions are unobservable, and quantifying it also requires distinguishing a property's underlying risk from the incentives created by its insurance contract. Our data and our model allow us to do this at the contract level: for millions of homes, we observe key contract terms, detailed measures of underlying property risk, and rich borrower and property characteristics. Combining these data with the model, we estimate how much households value protection from risk, the cost associated with moral hazard, and how much risk homeowners ultimately retain. We leave the technical details of the model and estimation to our paper and focus here on the economic intuition and main findings.

detail.abstract:
States unquestionably possess authority to investigate and prosecute violations of their criminal laws. But when the potential suspect is a federal law enforcement officer, difficult questions arise about both the scope of states’ authority and their practical ability to exercise it. Federal officers are not exempt from state investigation simply because they were acting under color of law. At the same time, federal agencies may control much of the evidence necessary for the state to determine whether prosecution is appropriate. States’ ability to investigate these potential crimes encounters serious practical barriers when federal agencies refuse to share evidence.

Courts and scholars have devoted virtually no attention to how states should investigate potential crimes by federal officers when federal agencies obstruct those investigations. This Article addresses that problem. Prompted by disputes between Minnesota and the federal government after federal agents shot three Minneapolis residents in early 2026, the Article examines the respective authority of state and federal governments when states seek to investigate federal officers. The Article makes three principal contributions. It first demonstrates that states retain authority to investigate crimes by federal officers even though agents may claim immunity from prosecution.

Next, the Article turns to a practical obstacle to states exercising that authority: access to evidence controlled by federal agencies. Existing doctrine governing demands for evidence is confusing and often too deferential to the whims of federal agencies. This Article argues that while federal regulations may establish procedures for responding to state requests, they cannot create a substantive privilege to withhold evidence.

Finally, the Article proposes a five-step framework for resolving federal-state disputes over investigative evidence. The framework acknowledges that federal agencies may occasionally have legitimate reasons to withhold evidence, while ensuring independent judicial review of agency refusals and appropriate consideration of states’ interest in enforcing their criminal laws.

detail.abstract: We introduce the Household Expectations Survey of the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye, which elicits 12-month-ahead expectations for inflation, the USD/TRY exchange rate, and house price growth after informing respondents of the latest official figures. Using the January-August 2026 waves, we document seven stylized facts. First, households expect inflation far above the official rates they are shown, although expectations and disagreement decline over the sample. Second, socioeconomic gradients differ across expectation domains and explain less than 5 percent of the variation in beliefs. Third, households that perceive domestic risks or expect food and rents to rise fastest hold markedly higher inflation expectations. Fourth, inflation, exchange rate, and house price expectations move together. Fifth, inflation expectations are positively associated with perceived inflation, expected exchange-rate depreciation, and expected house price growth. Sixth, higher inflation expectations characterize credit applicants and, at least as strongly, households deterred from borrowing. Finally, eight in ten respondents would invest spare cash in gold or real estate, but the share choosing time deposits more than doubles amid high interest rates.

detail.abstract: This research investigates the impact of natural disasters on foreign direct investment (FDI) in the United States, with a focus on county-level variations and sector-specific effects. While previous studies have explored the broader relationship between FDI and natural disasters at the national level, this study provides a fine-grained analysis within the U.S., using data from the Agricultural Foreign Investment Disclosure Act (AFIDA) and the Spatial Hazard Events and Losses Database for the United States (SHELDUS). We focus on agriculture, a sector highly vulnerable to environmental shocks, to identify heterogeneous disaster effects on foreign investment. Our results reveal that natural disasters reduce foreign-owned forestland and, under certain conditions, increase foreign-owned cropland-particularly in urban counties. Crop insurance does not cushion investment in the short run; instead, past insurance payouts are associated with increased investment in hazard-prone cropland, consistent with a dynamic expectations channel. These patterns show how disaster risk reshapes agricultural land use and how insurance acts as a dynamic expectation rather than an immediate shield.

detail.abstract: How do incumbent workers adjust their human capital when a new technology changes the value of existing skills? I study this question using quarterly résumé histories for 1.5 million U.S. workers from 2018 through 2025 and the public release of ChatGPT as a common shock. Treatment intensity is the pre-release AI exposure of a worker's occupation. Workers in more exposed occupations become substantially more likely to earn AI-related credentials after ChatGPT. This increase does not represent a broad expansion of training: the same workers reduce certification in adjacent technical fields, including data science and cloud/IT, and in other discretionary subjects such as marketing and finance, while safety and compliance credentials do not move and total certification does not increase. The response is therefore primarily a reallocation of human-capital investment across skills. Adjustment is stronger among postgraduates, workers with technical backgrounds, employees at large firms, workers with shorter tenure, and workers already employed in technology industries. Employer demand for AI skills subsequently rises more in exposed occupations, but worker certification begins to increase before this rise in vacancy demand becomes clearly detectable. The findings are consistent with workers reallocating skill investment in anticipation of technological change before changes in posted labor demand are fully visible.

detail.abstract: Firms differ substantially in the age structure of their workforces, even within similar industries and labor markets. We show that these differences in age structures are systematically related to firms' production needs and have important consequences for early-career workers' promotion and retention. We develop a model linking production needs to workforce age structure, promotion congestion, and worker retention, and test its predictions using Revelio's employer-employee data. We find that firms with greater reliance on abstract skills consistently employ older workforces, resulting in more top-heavy age structures. Early-career workers in top-heavy firms face weaker promotion prospects, report lower satisfaction with career opportunities, and exhibit lower retention. To isolate the effects of workforce aging unrelated to firms' labor demand, we exploit unexpected changes in workers' incentive to retire and show similar effects on promotion and retention. We further show that firms can mitigate these promotion and retention challenges through career development programs targeted at early-career workers, when those programs build firm-specific rather than general skills. Our findings position workforce age structure as an outcome of a tradeoff for firms between their skill needs and workforce renewal, and identify career development as one mechanism through which firms can manage the challenges.

detail.abstract: Improving access to agronomic information could enhance the livelihoods of hundreds of millions of smallholder farmers in low-and middle-income countries. Delivering timely, actionable advice remains a last-mile challenge. AI-powered chatbots offer a low-cost, scalable channel for personalized advice, and are increasingly being adopted by businesses and policymakers, yet there is a marked absence of causal evidence on their effects on farming practices. We conducted a pre-registered randomized controlled trial with 1,935 smallholder rice farmers in the Philippines and India over one production cycle. Treatment-arm farmers received an AI advisor on WhatsApp or Messenger, developed with local experts and promoting sustainable rice cultivation practices. Control-arm farmers received a similar conversational AI chatbot without agronomic content, isolating the added effect of agronomic information. AI advisory changed how farmers managed their farms. Deliberate practice changes increased by a fifth (+0.10 SD), and the quality of farming operations improved (+0.08 SD). Effects were concentrated on crop protection and problem response, which were also the most frequent topics in conversation logs. Treatment-arm farmers reported shifting toward more integrated management of pests, weeds, and diseases (+0.11 SD) and were more likely to adopt new practices in these areas (+0.10 SD) compared with control-arm farmers. Treatment also increased reported avoidance of crop-residue burning by 7 percentage points relative to control, but did not significantly affect the adoption of other targeted sustainable practices. We find no statistically significant effects on the adoption of technologies or inputs other than pesticides, or on costs or yields in that cycle. These findings suggest that AI advisory can improve management practices that farmers can adjust using resources at hand, particularly in response to time-sensitive problems, while on-demand information alone may not have transformative effects without more proactive use or access to complementary resources.

detail.abstract: This paper documents declines in the intra-household bargaining power and reproductive autonomy of currently married women in an affected minority community following targeted communal violence. I estimate the long-run effects of anti-Muslim riots in 2002 on Muslim women's bargaining power and reproductive autonomy using four rounds of India's National Family Health Survey (1998–2021) and a triple difference-in-differences design, comparing Muslim to non-Muslim women in Gujarat relative to other Indian states. Decision-making power over household purchases fell by 5.8 percentage points and over decisions about visiting family and friends by 5.3 percentage points, with declines present three and seventeen years after the riots, while the shift from concealable to male-controlled contraception is consistent with women losing private control over fertility. Gujarati Hindu women experienced even larger declines, so these estimates are the differential component of a larger Gujarat-wide decline, and they are not replicated by Muslim women in states bordering Gujarat. The impact of communal violence spread far beyond the immediate deaths, diminishing the independence of women in Gujarat for decades afterward.

detail.abstract:
A growing case law recognizes private damages claims for market manipulation. While prosecutors and enforcement authorities often focus on the manipulator's gains, private plaintiffs must establish losses. That requires an estimate of how much a manipulative act moved the price and for how long. Some courts have looked to a price path after the misconduct and concluded that the effect dissipated when the price reverted. However, because prices generally follow random walks, any path can drift above or below where it began for entirely random reasons. The finance and economics literature typically overcomes that random variation by averaging across many realized paths. But over longer horizons an average may be contaminated by unrelated news, and courts have insisted that plaintiffs identify the price impact of each manipulative episode.

This Article proposes a way through that tension. The price impact of manipulation is most clearly measurable in the immediate wake of each episode before random volatility and other news contaminates price paths. Following Ferrell and Saha (2007, 2012), I propose "forward-casting" the price impact of each manipulative event in a high-frequency, intraday event study with an overtime decay model that allows the price to converge back to the unaffected level. The decay model is based on the finance and economics literature, fitted separately to each episode, with no averaging. This yields an estimate of the but-for price of the asset at each point in time.

I apply this analysis to a series of SEC, CFTC and DOJ enforcement actions whose filings give the times of the alleged manipulation. In many episodes, the estimated distortion dissipates the same day as the manipulation. In others, the curve declines slowly, leading to a substantial amount of estimated losses to investors. Where the manipulation's price impact was fleeting, disgorgement of the defendant's gains may be preferred to compensating investor losses. On the other hand, where manipulation was longer lasting, investor losses can exceed the manipulator's gains many times over, and a remedy measured by gains alone may lead to under-deterrence.

detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Nonprofits recruiting skilled volunteers face a tradeoff in communicating task requirements. While more precise information about task requirements helps volunteers recognize a good fit, it can also discourage participation by revealing mismatches. We study how nonprofits should disclose task requirements to skilled volunteers who value both the intrinsic reward from participation and the match between their skills and the task requirements. 

Methodology/results: We develop an information-design model in which the nonprofit commits to a disclosure policy before task difficulty is realized, and sends a signal to a volunteer after observing it. The volunteer then uses this signal to decide whether to participate. We show that the optimal disclosure policy takes the form of a personalized interval test: it reveals only whether task difficulty lies in a volunteer-specific range. The policy selects the largest range that still induces acceptance, and raises the nonprofit's expected payoff by more than 27% relative to full and no disclosure policies while preserving each volunteer type's expected utility under no disclosure. We then study the case where the volunteers' skill levels are private information, and consider invitation-only interval policies in which volunteers report their skills and may participate only if invited. Within this class, we characterize an optimal incentive-compatible policy that deters misreporting by pooling some skill reports and adjusting the ranges across skill levels. The policy offers substantial participation gains and increases average volunteer welfare relative to no disclosure. Finally, we examine how the value of disclosure varies with volunteer composition and the distribution of task difficulty. 

Managerial implications: Nonprofits can substantially increase participation using disclosure policies that are easy to implement, without reducing volunteer welfare relative to no disclosure. Platforms using self-reported skills should design invitation rules jointly across skill levels so that volunteers cannot benefit from misrepresenting their expertise.

detail.abstract: Hybrid teamwork (HTW), combining virtual and face-to-face interaction through information technology, has become a cornerstone of today's organizations. The complexity of HTW requires a profound understanding to improve communication and effectiveness, whereas prior studies have been less integrated, providing only a partial understanding of HTW and its inconsistent effects. We approach these issues through sociotechnical theories that emphasize the integration of information technology with human factors. We propose a Hybrid Teamwork Comparative Model (HTWCM) based on communication by comparing and synthesizing five perspectives. This model connects fragmented knowledge to be more holistic. First, we delve into debates in these perspectives and reconceptualize them to indicate their unique contributions and limitations. Then, we compare and integrate them to construct HTWCM and pursue a holistic understanding of HTW for improvement. We further discuss the application of HTWCM to analyze the sociotechnical relationships and design HTW. We discuss future directions for sustainable HTW in ever-changing situations.

detail.abstract: Stack Overow lost roughly 95% of its monthly question volume between November 2022 and December 2025. This is a larger rate and drop than any digital service in the past twenty years, and it occurred while the platform was operating and solvent. In this paper I aggregate what the empirical literature has learned about why, read the 20252026 journalism against the peer-reviewed work that stops in early 2024, and argue that we should treat the shock as a case of demand substitution rather than the kind of free-riding problem the digitalcommons literature was built around. The empirical consensus is clear enough: generative AI drove a large, persistent drop in posting; the drop hit newcomers hardest and routine topics hardest; and what remains on the platform skews toward harder questions and longer code. The arguments that are still open whether we have reached a oor, whether agentic coding tools are a second shock in their own right, and what any of this does to the training data for the next generation of models are the ones worth working on. I compare the six studies on how they identify their eects, work through the Russian-language case because it carries most of the identication weight in the leading paper, and lay out a research agenda for anyone who wants to pick this up. The paper is a review and a position statement, not a new empirical contribution; all numbers I quote come from someone else's work and I say whose.

detail.abstract: Between September 2025 and April 2026, five specifications made identity, authority, intent, and payment authorization portable in agentic commerce. Read the schemas rather than the announcements, and the same two things are missing from every one of them: what a human did with a model's output, and which model produced it. This paper argues that the absence may persist rather than close, because whoever supplies the format in which such a record is recognized would hold a position from which to charge for reliance itself. That is offered as a hypothesis and tested against correspondent banking, the published accounts of firms that already have verification layers, and one counterexample in which the users own the facility. It closes with a dated prediction and the tests that would prove it wrong.
